Probability that all geological risk factors (trap, reservoir, seal, source, timing/migration) are present and effective. Expressed as percentage (0.00 to 100.00). Used to calculate risked resource estimates.
Name of the lead geophysicist responsible for seismic interpretation and depth conversion. Used for accountability and technical review.

business_glossary_term: Gas Initially in Place (GIIP) Unrisked Billion Cubic Feet
description: Unrisked estimate of original gas in place in billion cubic feet. Calculated from volumetric parameters before applying geological chance of success.

business_glossary_term: Gross Rock Volume (GRV) Million Cubic Feet
description: Total rock volume within the structural closure in million cubic feet. Calculated from seismic interpretation and depth structure maps in Petrel.
Average hydrocarbon saturation (1 minus water saturation) as a fraction (0.0 to 1.0). Estimated from analog well logs and petrophysical models.
Expected hydrocarbon phase in the prospect: oil, gas, condensate, or mixed. Drives economic evaluation and facility design assumptions.
Date when the G&G interpretation and prospect evaluation were completed. Used for tracking prospect vintage and re-evaluation cycles.
Maturity classification: lead (early stage, low confidence), prospect (G&G analysis complete), or drillable prospect (AFE approved, ready to drill).
Ratio of net reservoir thickness to gross interval thickness. Derived from analog well log analysis and petrophysical modeling. Range 0.0 to 1.0.
Average reservoir porosity as a fraction (0.0 to 1.0). Estimated from seismic inversion, analog wells, and core data. Key input for STOIIP/GIIP calculation.

business_glossary_term: Petroleum Resources Management System (PRMS) Resource Classification
description: SPE PRMS classification of the prospect resource: 1P (proved), 2P (proved plus probable), 3P (proved plus probable plus possible), contingent, prospective, or unrecoverable. Used for SEC reserves disclosure.
Externally-known unique alphanumeric code assigned to the prospect for tracking across Landmark DecisionSpace and Schlumberger Petrel systems. Used in AFE and JIB documentation.
Business name assigned to the prospect for identification and communication purposes. Human-readable label used in exploration planning and AFE documentation.

Current lifecycle status of the prospect: identified (initial screening), evaluated (G&G analysis complete), matured (ready for drilling decision), drilled (well spudded), or abandoned (dropped from portfolio).
Probability that reservoir quality (porosity, permeability) is adequate for commercial production (0.0 to 1.0). Component of geological chance of success calculation.
Probability that an effective seal (cap rock) is present to prevent hydrocarbon migration (0.0 to 1.0). Component of geological chance of success calculation.
Probability that mature source rock is present and has generated sufficient hydrocarbons (0.0 to 1.0). Component of geological chance of success calculation.

business_glossary_term: Stock Tank Oil Initially in Place (STOIIP) Unrisked Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent
description: Unrisked estimate of original oil in place in million barrels of oil equivalent. Calculated from volumetric parameters before applying geological chance of success.
Areal extent of the structural closure at the spill point in acres. Key input for volumetric resource calculation and STOIIP/GIIP estimation.
Geographic latitude coordinate of the prospect surface location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping and regulatory filing.
Geographic longitude coordinate of the prospect surface location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping and regulatory filing.

business_glossary_term: Target Depth True Vertical Depth (TVD) Feet
description: True vertical depth to the top of the reservoir target in feet below surface or seabed. Used for drilling cost estimation and well planning.
Probability that hydrocarbon generation, migration, and trap formation occurred in the correct sequence (0.0 to 1.0). Component of geological chance of success calculation.
Probability that a valid hydrocarbon trap exists (0.0 to 1.0). Component of geological chance of success calculation.
Classification of the hydrocarbon trapping mechanism: structural (anticline, fault block), stratigraphic (pinchout, unconformity), combination, or hydrodynamic.
Timestamp when the prospect record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.
Water depth at the prospect surface location in feet. Applicable for offshore prospects. Used for drilling cost estimation and rig selection.
Unique identifier for the prospect resource estimate record. Primary key for this transactional evaluation entity.
Reference to the prospect being evaluated. Links this resource estimate to the specific exploration prospect or play.
Reference to the newer estimate version that supersedes this record. Enables version chain tracking and audit trail for estimate evolution.
Probability that sufficient hydrocarbon charge has migrated into the trap. Individual geological risk factor component.
Free-text field for evaluator notes, assumptions, data quality observations, and technical commentary supporting the resource estimate.
System timestamp when this resource estimate record was first created in the database. Supports audit trail and data lineage.
Date when this resource estimate was prepared. Represents the principal business event timestamp for this evaluation record.
Current lifecycle status of this resource estimate version. Active is current, superseded indicates newer version exists, archived for historical record, withdrawn if invalidated.
Version number of this resource estimate. Multiple versions per prospect track evaluation evolution over time as new data becomes available.

business_glossary_term: Estimated Ultimate Recovery (EUR) One P (1P) Barrel of Oil Equivalent (BOE)
description: Proved reserves (1P) estimated ultimate recovery in barrels of oil equivalent. Represents recoverable volumes with reasonable certainty per SEC and SPE-PRMS standards.

business_glossary_term: Estimated Ultimate Recovery (EUR) Two P (2P) Barrel of Oil Equivalent (BOE)
description: Proved plus probable reserves (2P) estimated ultimate recovery in barrels of oil equivalent. Represents best estimate of recoverable volumes per SPE-PRMS standards.

business_glossary_term: Estimated Ultimate Recovery (EUR) Three P (3P) Barrel of Oil Equivalent (BOE)
description: Proved plus probable plus possible reserves (3P) estimated ultimate recovery in barrels of oil equivalent. Represents high-side estimate of recoverable volumes per SPE-PRMS standards.
Technical methodology used to derive the resource estimate. Volumetric uses reservoir volume calculations, analog uses comparable field data, simulation uses reservoir modeling software.
Name of the geoscientist or engineer who prepared this resource estimate. Supports audit trail and technical accountability.

business_glossary_term: Expected Monetary Value (EMV) United States Dollars (USD)
description: Risk-weighted net present value of the prospect calculated as NPV multiplied by geological chance of success. Key metric for portfolio optimization and investment decisions.
Composite probability that all geological risk factors are favorable and prospect contains commercial hydrocarbons. Calculated using risk methodology (multiplicative or additive).

business_glossary_term: Gas Initially In Place (GIIP) High Case Billion Cubic Feet (BCF)
description: High case (P10) estimate of original gas in place in billion cubic feet. Represents optimistic scenario for gas prospects.

business_glossary_term: Gas Initially In Place (GIIP) Low Case Billion Cubic Feet (BCF)
description: Low case (P90) estimate of original gas in place in billion cubic feet. Represents conservative scenario for gas prospects.

business_glossary_term: Gas Initially In Place (GIIP) Mid Case Billion Cubic Feet (BCF)
description: Mid case (P50) estimate of original gas in place in billion cubic feet. Represents best estimate scenario for gas prospects.
System timestamp when this resource estimate record was last modified. Supports audit trail and change tracking.
Date when peer review was completed. Tracks evaluation lifecycle and supports audit requirements.
Current status of technical peer review process for this resource estimate. Ensures quality control and technical governance before investment decisions.
Name of senior geoscientist or engineer who conducted peer review of this resource estimate. Supports technical accountability and audit trail.

business_glossary_term: Petroleum Resources Management System (PRMS) Resource Category
description: SPE-PRMS 2018 classification of resource maturity. Prospective resources are undiscovered, contingent resources are discovered but not yet commercial, reserves are discovered and commercial.

business_glossary_term: Petroleum Resources Management System (PRMS) Resource Subclass
description: Detailed SPE-PRMS sub-classification. For prospective: play, lead, prospect. For reserves: PDP (proved developed producing), PDNP (proved developed non-producing), PUD (proved undeveloped).
High case recovery factor as percentage of OOIP or OGIP that can be economically produced. Optimistic estimate of reservoir producibility.
Low case recovery factor as percentage of OOIP or OGIP that can be economically produced. Conservative estimate of reservoir producibility.
Mid case recovery factor as percentage of OOIP or OGIP that can be economically produced. Best estimate of reservoir producibility.
Probability that reservoir-quality rock is present at the prospect location. Individual geological risk factor component for chance of success calculation.
Probability that reservoir rock has sufficient porosity and permeability for commercial production. Individual geological risk factor component.
Method used to combine individual geological risk factors into composite chance of success. Multiplicative multiplies all factors, additive uses weighted sum, hybrid combines both approaches.

business_glossary_term: Risk-Weighted Net Present Value (NPV) United States Dollars (USD)
description: Discounted cash flow value adjusted for geological and commercial risks. Used for economic ranking and capital allocation decisions.

business_glossary_term: Risked Resource High Case Barrel of Oil Equivalent (BOE)
description: High case recoverable resource volume adjusted by geological chance of success. Calculated as EUR high case multiplied by composite geological risk factor.

business_glossary_term: Risked Resource Low Case Barrel of Oil Equivalent (BOE)
description: Low case recoverable resource volume adjusted by geological chance of success. Calculated as EUR low case multiplied by composite geological risk factor.

business_glossary_term: Risked Resource Mid Case Barrel of Oil Equivalent (BOE)
description: Mid case recoverable resource volume adjusted by geological chance of success. Calculated as EUR mid case multiplied by composite geological risk factor.
Probability that cap rock or seal is present and effective to prevent hydrocarbon migration. Individual geological risk factor component.

business_glossary_term: Stock Tank Oil Initially In Place (STOIIP) High Case Barrels (BBL)
description: High case (P10) estimate of original oil in place in stock tank barrels. Represents optimistic scenario with 10% probability of exceeding this volume.

business_glossary_term: Stock Tank Oil Initially In Place (STOIIP) Low Case Barrels (BBL)
description: Low case (P90) estimate of original oil in place in stock tank barrels. Represents conservative scenario with 90% probability of exceeding this volume.

business_glossary_term: Stock Tank Oil Initially In Place (STOIIP) Mid Case Barrels (BBL)
description: Mid case (P50) estimate of original oil in place in stock tank barrels. Represents best estimate scenario with 50% probability of exceeding this volume.
Probability that hydrocarbon generation, migration, and trap formation occurred in correct sequence. Individual geological risk factor component.
Probability that structural or stratigraphic trap is present and intact to contain hydrocarbons. Individual geological risk factor component.

Mole percentage of methane (C1) in the feedstock composition. Part of the hydrocarbon composition profile used for process simulation and yield optimization.
Average molecular weight of the feedstock material in grams per mole (g/mol). Used for mass balance calculations, process simulation in Aspen HYSYS, and stoichiometric analysis in chemical reactions.
Nitrogen content of the feedstock measured in parts per million (ppm). Nitrogen compounds can act as catalyst poisons in petrochemical processes and must be monitored for process optimization.
Research Octane Number (RON) of the feedstock material, a measure of anti-knock performance in gasoline blending. Applicable to naphtha and gasoline-range feedstocks used in petrochemical operations.

Percentage of olefinic (unsaturated) hydrocarbons in the feedstock composition. Olefins are key intermediates in petrochemical manufacturing (ethylene, propylene) and affect process stability and product yield.
Percentage of paraffinic (saturated) hydrocarbons in the feedstock composition. Paraffins are stable, non-reactive hydrocarbons that influence feedstock cracking behavior and product distribution.
Pour point of the feedstock material in degrees Fahrenheit, the lowest temperature at which the material will flow under specified conditions. Important for cold weather operations and storage.
Mole percentage of propane (C3) in the feedstock composition. Key input for propylene production and LPG processing operations.

Quality classification of the feedstock material based on composition specifications, purity, and conformance to contractual or industry standards. Premium grade feedstocks command higher prices and yield better conversion rates.
reference: API Standards, ISO Quality Management Standards

business_glossary_term: Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP) in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI)
description: Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP) of the feedstock material measured in pounds per square inch (psi). A standard measure of volatility for petroleum liquids, critical for EPA emissions compliance and storage safety.

value_regex: Field Production|Refinery Output|Import|Third-Party Supplier|Joint Venture|Internal Transfer
description: Origin classification of the feedstock material indicating whether it is produced internally, purchased externally, or transferred from joint venture operations.
Specific gravity of the feedstock material at standard conditions (60°F/15.6°C). Used for volume-to-mass conversions and process engineering calculations.

Sulfur content of the feedstock measured in parts per million (ppm). Critical for environmental compliance (EPA emissions standards), catalyst performance, and downstream product quality in petrochemical manufacturing.
reference: EPA Clean Air Act, ASTM D4294, ISO 8754

business_glossary_term: Total Acid Number (TAN) in Milligrams Potassium Hydroxide per Gram
description: Total Acid Number (TAN) of the feedstock, measured in milligrams of potassium hydroxide (KOH) required to neutralize one gram of the material. Indicates acidity level and corrosion potential in processing equipment.

business_glossary_term: Vapor Pressure (Pounds per Square Inch Absolute)
description: Vapor pressure of the feedstock material at standard conditions, measured in pounds per square inch absolute (psia). Critical for storage tank design, transportation safety, and process equipment sizing.
Kinematic viscosity of the feedstock material at standard temperature, measured in centistokes (cSt). Affects pumping requirements, heat transfer efficiency, and process equipment design.
Water content of the feedstock measured in parts per million (ppm). Excess water can cause corrosion, catalyst deactivation, and process inefficiencies in petrochemical manufacturing.

description: Target density specification in kilograms per cubic meter (kg/m³) at a specified temperature for the blended product. Used for volume-to-mass conversions and quality control.
reference: ASTM D4052 - Standard Test Method for Density, Relative Density, and API Gravity of Liquids by Digital Density Meter

description: Target flash point specification in degrees Celsius for the blended product. Critical safety property for handling, storage, and transportation.
reference: ASTM D93 - Standard Test Methods for Flash Point by Pensky-Martens Closed Cup Tester

description: Target freeze point specification in degrees Celsius for jet fuel blends. Critical for aviation fuel performance at high altitudes and cold climates.
reference: ASTM D5972 - Standard Test Method for Freezing Point of Aviation Fuels (Automatic Phase Transition Method)

description: Target Motor Octane Number (MON) specification for the blended gasoline product. Used in conjunction with RON to determine anti-knock index.
reference: ASTM D2700 - Standard Test Method for Motor Octane Number of Spark-Ignition Engine Fuel

description: Target Research Octane Number (RON) specification for the blended gasoline product. Critical quality property for spark-ignition engine fuel performance.
reference: ASTM D2699 - Standard Test Method for Research Octane Number of Spark-Ignition Engine Fuel

business_glossary_term: Target Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP) in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI)
description: Target Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP) specification in pounds per square inch (psi) for the blended gasoline product. Controls evaporative emissions and seasonal volatility requirements.
reference: ASTM D323 - Standard Test Method for Vapor Pressure of Petroleum Products (Reid Method)

description: Target sulfur content specification in parts per million (ppm) for the blended product. Critical for Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) emissions compliance and Hydrodesulfurization (HDS) operations.
reference: EPA Tier 3 Gasoline Sulfur Standards (40 CFR 80.195)

description: Target kinematic viscosity specification in centistokes (cSt) at a specified temperature for the blended product. Important for fuel oils and lubricants.
reference: ASTM D445 - Standard Test Method for Kinematic Viscosity of Transparent and Opaque Liquids

description: Unique identifier for the crude assay record. Primary key for the crude assay master data product.
Reference to the crude oil grade that this assay characterizes. Links to the crude grade master in the product domain.

Foreign key linking to hse.hazardous_substance. Business justification: Crude assays identify H2S content, NORM levels, and hazardous components. Safety data sheets, Tier II reporting, and worker exposure assessments require assay-to-substance linkage for hazard classific

Foreign key linking to commercial.price_differential. Business justification: Crude assay properties (API gravity, sulfur content, TAN) directly determine price differentials versus benchmark. Essential for crude valuation, procurement pricing, and margin optimization.
API gravity of the crude oil, measured in degrees API. Key indicator of crude density and quality; higher API gravity indicates lighter, more valuable crude. Typical range 10-50 degrees API.
reference: API MPMS Chapter 11.1 - Volume Correction Factors

description: Aromatic hydrocarbon content of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent (from SARA analysis: Saturates, Aromatics, Resins, Asphaltenes). Aromatic content affects product quality (cetane, smoke point) and processing severity requirements.
reference: ASTM D2007 - Standard Test Method for Characteristic Groups in Rubber Extender and Processing Oils by the Clay-Gel Absorption Chromatographic Method (SARA Analysis)

description: Asphaltene content of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent. Asphaltenes are heavy, polar molecules that cause fouling, coking, and stability issues. High asphaltene content affects crude compatibility for blending and requires careful processing.
reference: ASTM D6560 - Standard Test Method for Determination of Asphaltenes (Heptane Insolubles) in Crude Petroleum and Petroleum Products

description: Date when the crude oil sample was assayed or when the assay data was published. Used for assay currency and validity tracking.
reference: ASTM D4057 - Standard Practice for Manual Sampling of Petroleum and Petroleum Products

description: Name of the laboratory or organization that performed the crude assay analysis. Used for assay quality validation and traceability.
reference: ISO/IEC 17025 - General Requirements for the Competence of Testing and Calibration Laboratories

description: Business name or identifier for this crude assay, typically including crude grade name and source location (e.g., 'Brent North Sea 2023', 'WTI Cushing Q1').
Reference number or document identifier for the detailed crude assay laboratory report. Links to the full assay documentation including all test results and distillation curves.
Current lifecycle status of the assay record. Active assays are used for refinery planning and optimization; superseded assays are retained for historical analysis.
Version identifier for this assay. Crude assays are updated periodically as crude quality varies; version tracks the iteration.

Conradson Carbon Residue (CCR) of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent. Indicates coke-forming tendency and asphaltene content. High CCR crude yields more residue and requires coking or residue upgrading capacity. Used for FCC feed quality assessment.
reference: ASTM D189 - Standard Test Method for Conradson Carbon Residue of Petroleum Products; ASTM D4530 - Standard Test Method for Determination of Carbon Residue (Micro Method)

description: Calculated cetane index of the diesel fraction from the crude assay. Indicates diesel ignition quality; higher cetane index means better diesel quality. Used for crude valuation and diesel blending optimization.
reference: ASTM D976 - Standard Test Method for Calculated Cetane Index of Distillate Fuels; ASTM D4737 - Standard Test Method for Calculated Cetane Index by Four Variable Equation

description: Timestamp when this crude assay record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.
Volume percent yield of diesel cut (typically 520-650°F / 271-343°C) from crude distillation. Diesel is a high-value middle distillate product; yield is a key crude valuation factor.
reference: API Technical Data Book - Petroleum Refining; Aspen HYSYS Process Simulation Standards

description: Laboratory distillation method used to generate the crude assay distillation curve. TBP (True Boiling Point) provides the most detailed cut-by-cut yield data for refinery simulation. ASTM D86 is a simpler atmospheric distillation. ASTM D2892 and D5236 are standard crude assay distillation methods.
reference: ASTM D2892 - Standard Test Method for Distillation of Crude Petroleum (15-Theoretical Plate Column); ASTM D5236 - Standard Test Method for Distillation of Heavy Hydrocarbon Mixtures (Vacuum Potstill Method)

description: Flash point of the crude oil in degrees Celsius. Lowest temperature at which vapors ignite when exposed to an ignition source. Critical for HSE classification, storage tank design, and transportation safety (OSHA, NFPA, DOT regulations).
reference: ASTM D93 - Standard Test Methods for Flash Point by Pensky-Martens Closed Cup Tester; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.106; NFPA 30

description: Freeze point of the kerosene/jet fuel fraction, measured in degrees Celsius. Critical specification for jet fuel to prevent fuel system icing at high altitude. ASTM D1655 Jet A specification requires maximum -40°C freeze point.
reference: ASTM D2386 - Standard Test Method for Freezing Point of Aviation Fuels; ASTM D1655 - Standard Specification for Aviation Turbine Fuels

description: Volume percent yield of heavy naphtha cut (typically 180-380°F / 82-193°C) from crude distillation. Heavy naphtha is primary feedstock for catalytic reforming to produce high-octane reformate and hydrogen.
reference: API Technical Data Book - Petroleum Refining; Aspen HYSYS Process Simulation Standards

description: Hydrogen content of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent. Higher hydrogen content indicates more paraffinic crude with better product quality potential. Used in refinery hydrogen balance calculations.
reference: ASTM D5291 - Standard Test Methods for Instrumental Determination of Carbon, Hydrogen, and Nitrogen in Petroleum Products and Lubricants

business_glossary_term: Iron Content in Parts Per Million (ppm)
description: Iron (Fe) content in the crude oil, measured in parts per million (ppm). Iron indicates contamination from pipelines, storage tanks, or production equipment. High iron content can foul heat exchangers and poison catalysts.
reference: ASTM D5863 - Standard Test Methods for Determination of Nickel, Vanadium, Iron, and Sodium in Crude Oils and Residual Fuels by Flame Atomic Absorption Spectrometry

description: Volume percent yield of kerosene cut (typically 380-520°F / 193-271°C) from crude distillation. Kerosene is feedstock for jet fuel and heating oil production.
reference: API Technical Data Book - Petroleum Refining; Aspen HYSYS Process Simulation Standards

description: Volume percent yield of light naphtha cut (typically C5-180°F / C5-82°C) from crude distillation. Light naphtha is feedstock for isomerization and reforming to produce high-octane gasoline blendstock.
reference: API Technical Data Book - Petroleum Refining; Aspen HYSYS Process Simulation Standards

description: Timestamp when this crude assay record was last modified. Used for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

business_glossary_term: Nickel Content in Parts Per Million (ppm)
description: Nickel (Ni) content in the crude oil, measured in parts per million (ppm). Nickel and vanadium are catalyst poisons in FCC and hydroprocessing units. High-metal crudes require specialized processing or blending to reduce metal content.
reference: ASTM D5863 - Standard Test Methods for Determination of Nickel, Vanadium, Iron, and Sodium in Crude Oils and Residual Fuels by Flame Atomic Absorption Spectrometry

business_glossary_term: Nitrogen Content in Weight Parts Per Million (wt ppm)
description: Total nitrogen content of the crude oil, measured in weight ppm. Nitrogen compounds are catalyst poisons in hydrotreating and hydrocracking units and contribute to NOx emissions. High-nitrogen crudes require additional hydrotreating capacity.
reference: ASTM D4629 - Standard Test Method for Trace Nitrogen in Liquid Petroleum Hydrocarbons by Syringe/Inlet Oxidative Combustion and Chemiluminescence Detection

description: Pour point of the crude oil in degrees Celsius. Lowest temperature at which the crude will flow under gravity. Critical for cold-weather storage, pipeline transport, and tank heating requirements.
reference: ASTM D97 - Standard Test Method for Pour Point of Petroleum Products

description: Resin content of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent (from SARA analysis). Resins are polar compounds that contribute to crude stability and asphaltene solubility. High resin content can cause processing issues.
reference: ASTM D2007 - Standard Test Method for Characteristic Groups in Rubber Extender and Processing Oils by the Clay-Gel Absorption Chromatographic Method (SARA Analysis)

business_glossary_term: Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP) in Pounds per Square Inch (psi)
description: Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP) of the crude oil, measured in psi at 100°F. Indicates volatility and light-end content. High RVP crude requires vapor recovery systems and affects storage tank design. Also used for gasoline blending RVP compliance (EPA seasonal RVP limits).
reference: ASTM D323 - Standard Test Method for Vapor Pressure of Petroleum Products (Reid Method); EPA 40 CFR Part 80 Subpart E - RVP Standards for Gasoline

business_glossary_term: Salt Content in Pounds per Thousand Barrels (PTB)
description: Salt content of the crude oil, measured in pounds per thousand barrels (PTB). High salt content causes corrosion and fouling in crude distillation units. Crude desalting targets <1 PTB to protect downstream equipment.
reference: ASTM D3230 - Standard Test Method for Salts in Crude Oil (Electrometric Method); API RP 571 - Damage Mechanisms Affecting Fixed Equipment in the Refining Industry

description: Saturate (paraffin and naphthene) content of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent (from SARA analysis). High saturate content indicates better quality crude with higher diesel and lube oil yield potential.
reference: ASTM D2007 - Standard Test Method for Characteristic Groups in Rubber Extender and Processing Oils by the Clay-Gel Absorption Chromatographic Method (SARA Analysis)

description: Smoke point of the kerosene fraction, measured in millimeters. Indicates aromatic content and combustion quality of jet fuel. Higher smoke point means lower aromatics and better jet fuel quality. ASTM D1655 jet fuel specification requires minimum 25mm smoke point.
reference: ASTM D1322 - Standard Test Method for Smoke Point of Kerosene and Aviation Turbine Fuel; ASTM D1655 - Standard Specification for Aviation Turbine Fuels

description: Geographic origin or production field of the crude oil sample (e.g., 'North Sea', 'Permian Basin', 'Saudi Arabia'). Used for crude sourcing and logistics planning.
Specific gravity of the crude oil at 60°F/60°F (dimensionless ratio). Alternative density measure to API gravity, used in some international markets and process simulations.
reference: ASTM D1298 - Standard Test Method for Density, Relative Density, or API Gravity of Crude Petroleum

description: Total sulfur content of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent. Critical for refinery processing (HDS unit sizing), product quality (diesel/gasoline sulfur specs), and environmental compliance (EPA Tier 3 standards). Sweet crude <0.5%, sour crude >0.5%.
reference: ASTM D4294 - Standard Test Method for Sulfur in Petroleum by Energy Dispersive X-ray Fluorescence; EPA Tier 3 Gasoline Sulfur Standards

business_glossary_term: Total Acid Number (TAN) in Milligrams Potassium Hydroxide per Gram (mg KOH/g)
description: Total Acid Number (TAN) measured in mg KOH/g. Indicates naphthenic acid content; high TAN crude (>0.5) causes corrosion in refinery units (CDU/VDU overhead systems, heat exchangers). Critical for metallurgy selection and corrosion management.
reference: ASTM D664 - Standard Test Method for Acid Number of Petroleum Products by Potentiometric Titration; NACE SP0403 - Avoiding Caustic Stress Corrosion Cracking of Carbon Steel Refinery Equipment

description: Volume percent yield of vacuum residue (typically 1050°F+ / 566°C+) from vacuum distillation. Vacuum residue is the heaviest fraction, used for asphalt, fuel oil, or fed to coking/residue upgrading units. High residue yield reduces refinery margin.
reference: API Technical Data Book - Petroleum Refining; Aspen HYSYS Process Simulation Standards

business_glossary_term: Vanadium Content in Parts Per Million (ppm)
description: Vanadium (V) content in the crude oil, measured in parts per million (ppm). Vanadium is a catalyst poison and causes high-temperature corrosion in furnaces and boilers. Critical for FCC catalyst selection and residue upgrading economics.
reference: ASTM D5863 - Standard Test Methods for Determination of Nickel, Vanadium, Iron, and Sodium in Crude Oils and Residual Fuels by Flame Atomic Absorption Spectrometry

business_glossary_term: Vacuum Gas Oil (VGO) Yield Volume Percent (vol%)
description: Volume percent yield of vacuum gas oil (VGO) cut (typically 650-1050°F / 343-566°C) from vacuum distillation. VGO is primary feedstock for FCC and hydrocracking units to produce gasoline and diesel.
reference: API Technical Data Book - Petroleum Refining; Aspen HYSYS Process Simulation Standards

description: Kinematic viscosity of the crude oil at 100°C, measured in centistokes (cSt). Used for viscosity-temperature relationship modeling and high-temperature process unit design.
reference: ASTM D445 - Standard Test Method for Kinematic Viscosity of Transparent and Opaque Liquids

description: Kinematic viscosity of the crude oil at 40°C, measured in centistokes (cSt). Affects pumpability, pipeline transport, and heat exchanger design. Heavy crudes have higher viscosity.
reference: ASTM D445 - Standard Test Method for Kinematic Viscosity of Transparent and Opaque Liquids

description: Water and sediment content of the crude oil, expressed as volume percent. Affects crude valuation (water is non-saleable), desalter performance, and corrosion risk. Custody transfer specifications typically require <0.5% water.
reference: ASTM D4007 - Standard Test Method for Water and Sediment in Crude Oil by the Centrifuge Method; API MPMS Chapter 10 - Sediment and Water

description: Paraffin wax content of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent. High wax content affects pour point, pipeline flow, and cold-weather operability. Waxy crudes may require heating or dewaxing for transportation and processing.
reference: ASTM D721 - Standard Test Method for Oil Content of Petroleum Waxes

description: Unique identifier for the feedstock blend record. Primary key for the feedstock blend entity.

The actual total volume of the feedstock blend in barrels (BBL) that was processed through the target unit, measured upon completion or during operations.
The name or identifier of the refinery operations manager, process engineer, or authorized personnel who approved this feedstock blend for execution.
The date and time when this feedstock blend was formally approved for execution by authorized refinery personnel.

The weighted average API gravity of the feedstock blend, a measure of petroleum liquid density relative to water. Higher API gravity indicates lighter, less dense crude oil. Calculated based on component crude grades and their volume fractions.
reference: API MPMS Chapter 11.1 - Volume Correction Factors

description: The date when the feedstock blend processing or feeding to the target unit was completed or is scheduled to complete.
The weighted average flash point temperature of the feedstock blend in degrees Celsius, the lowest temperature at which vapors will ignite. Critical for HSE compliance and safe handling procedures.
reference: ASTM D93 - Flash Point, OSHA 29 CFR 1910.106

business_glossary_term: Blend Metals Content in Parts Per Million (PPM)
description: The weighted average total metals content (vanadium, nickel, iron) of the feedstock blend expressed in parts per million. Metals can cause catalyst deactivation and fouling in refinery process units.
Human-readable name or designation for this feedstock blend, used for operational identification and scheduling purposes.

business_glossary_term: Blend Nitrogen Content in Parts Per Million (PPM)
description: The weighted average nitrogen content of the feedstock blend expressed in parts per million. Nitrogen compounds can poison catalysts in downstream units such as FCC and hydrotreating units.
Externally-known unique business identifier or code assigned to this feedstock blend for tracking and reference in refinery operations and scheduling systems.

The weighted average pour point temperature of the feedstock blend in degrees Celsius, representing the lowest temperature at which the blend will flow. Important for storage and transportation planning.

business_glossary_term: Blend Salt Content in Pounds per Thousand Barrels (PTB)
description: The weighted average salt content of the feedstock blend expressed in pounds per thousand barrels. High salt content can cause corrosion and fouling in crude distillation units and requires desalting operations.

business_glossary_term: Blend Sediment Content in Volume Percent (VOL%)
description: The weighted average sediment content of the feedstock blend expressed as volume percentage. Sediment can cause fouling and operational issues in refinery equipment.
The date when the feedstock blend processing or feeding to the target unit began or is scheduled to begin.

Current lifecycle status of the feedstock blend. Planned indicates the blend recipe is designed but not yet approved, approved indicates ready for execution, in progress indicates currently being blended or fed to the unit, completed indicates the blend has been fully processed, cancelled indicates the blend was terminated before completion, and on hold indicates temporary suspension.

business_glossary_term: Blend Sulfur Content in Weight Percent (WT%)
description: The weighted average sulfur content of the feedstock blend expressed as weight percentage. Critical for HDS unit planning, EPA emissions compliance, and product quality specifications.
reference: API MPMS Chapter 11.1, EPA Clean Air Act

description: The weighted average Total Acid Number (TAN) of the feedstock blend, measured in milligrams of potassium hydroxide per gram of sample. TAN indicates the acidity and corrosivity of the crude oil, critical for refinery equipment integrity and corrosion management.
The precise date and time when the feedstock blend was initiated or executed in the refinery operations, representing the principal business event timestamp for this blend.

Classification of the feedstock blend based on its purpose and composition. Crude blend represents primary crude oil mixtures, intermediate blend represents processed stream mixtures, feedstock optimization represents cost or yield optimized recipes, emergency blend represents contingency blends, test blend represents experimental formulations, and standard recipe represents pre-approved recurring blends.

The weighted average kinematic viscosity of the feedstock blend measured in centistokes at a standard temperature (typically 40°C or 100°C). Viscosity affects pumping, heating, and processing requirements.

business_glossary_term: Blend Water Content in Volume Percent (VOL%)
description: The weighted average water content of the feedstock blend expressed as volume percentage. Water content affects processing efficiency and must be removed through desalting and dehydration operations.

The primary business driver or reason for creating this specific feedstock blend. Cost optimization indicates minimizing feedstock cost, yield optimization indicates maximizing valuable product yields, quality compliance indicates meeting product specifications, feedstock availability indicates working with available crude grades, contract obligation indicates fulfilling supply agreements, and operational constraint indicates adapting to refinery limitations.

Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, quality observations, or other relevant information about this feedstock blend that may be useful for refinery operations and future reference.
The date and time when this feedstock blend record was first created in the system, used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

business_glossary_term: Estimated Margin in United States Dollars (USD)
description: The estimated gross margin in USD from processing this feedstock blend, calculated as estimated product value minus estimated processing cost. Key metric for blend selection and refinery profitability analysis.

business_glossary_term: Estimated Processing Cost in United States Dollars (USD)
description: The estimated total cost in USD to process this feedstock blend through the target unit, including feedstock acquisition cost, energy consumption, catalyst usage, and operational expenses. Used for economic evaluation and margin analysis.

business_glossary_term: Estimated Product Value in United States Dollars (USD)
description: The estimated total market value in USD of the refined products expected from processing this feedstock blend, based on current market prices and target yield slate. Used for margin calculation and economic optimization.
The date and time when this feedstock blend record was last updated or modified, used for audit trail and change tracking.

A calculated score (typically 0-100) representing how well this feedstock blend achieves the blending objectives (cost, yield, quality) compared to alternative blend recipes. Higher scores indicate better optimization performance.
The total planned volume of the feedstock blend in barrels (BBL) to be processed through the target unit during the defined processing period.

Indicates whether the feedstock blend meets all required quality specifications and regulatory standards for processing in the target unit. Compliant indicates all specifications met, non-compliant indicates one or more specifications violated, pending review indicates awaiting quality assurance approval, conditionally approved indicates approved with operational restrictions, and requires adjustment indicates blend recipe needs modification.
reference: API Refining Standards, EPA Clean Air Act

description: The name of the operational system that originated this feedstock blend record, such as Aspen HYSYS process simulation system, refinery planning system, or DCS control system.
The target percentage yield of middle distillates (diesel, jet fuel, kerosene) expected from processing this feedstock blend, used for product slate planning.
The target percentage yield of light ends (LPG, propane, butane) expected from processing this feedstock blend, used for product slate planning and yield optimization.
The target percentage yield of naphtha expected from processing this feedstock blend, used for gasoline blending and petrochemical feedstock planning.
The target percentage yield of residue (heavy fuel oil, asphalt, vacuum residue) expected from processing this feedstock blend, used for downstream unit planning and product slate optimization.
The difference between planned and actual total volume in barrels, calculated as actual minus planned. Positive values indicate over-processing, negative values indicate under-processing.

description: SAP SD sales organization code to which this account is assigned. Defines the legal entity responsible for the sale, the applicable pricing conditions, and the revenue booking entity for financial consolidation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Sales Organization Structure; IFRS 15 Revenue Recognition

description: Indicates whether the counterparty associated with this account has been screened against applicable sanctions lists (OFAC SDN, EU Consolidated List, UN Sanctions). True = screened and cleared. False = not yet screened or screening pending.
reference: OFAC Sanctions Regulations; EU Sanctions Compliance; FATF Guidelines

description: Date on which the account status was last changed (e.g., from active to suspended, or from pending to active). Critical for SOX audit compliance and temporal status tracking in the Silver layer.
reference: SOX Section 404 Audit Trail; SAP S/4HANA SD Change Management

description: Business reason code or description explaining the most recent account status change (e.g., credit limit breach, KYC expiry, counterparty request, sanctions flag, commercial closure). Supports audit trail and compliance reporting.
reference: SOX Section 404; SAP S/4HANA SD Change Management; OFAC Compliance

description: Tax classification assigned to this account in SAP FI/SD, determining applicable VAT, excise duty, and withholding tax treatment for transactions. Varies by counterparty jurisdiction and product type.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Tax Management; IFRS/GAAP Tax Accounting; EPA Excise Tax Regulations

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the account record in the enterprise data platform. Conforms to ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change data capture, incremental processing, and audit trail.
reference: SOX Section 404; ISO 8601; SAP S/4HANA Audit Log

description: Value Added Tax (VAT) or equivalent indirect tax registration number of the counterparty. Required for tax invoice compliance, cross-border transaction reporting, and VAT reclaim processing.
reference: IFRS/GAAP Tax Reporting; EU VAT Directive; SAP S/4HANA FI Tax

business_glossary_term: Volume Commitment in Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
description: Contracted minimum or nominated daily volume commitment for this account expressed in Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD). Applicable for term offtake accounts. Used for production planning, logistics scheduling, and take-or-pay obligation tracking.
reference: API Measurement Standards; FERC Gas Tariff Volume Commitments; SAP S/4HANA SD Contracts

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each account hierarchy relationship record in the Oil Gas customer domain. Serves as the primary key for the account_hierarchy data product.
reference: COPAS Accounting Standards; SAP S/4HANA SD/FI Module

description: Identifier of the child (subsidiary or affiliate) account in the corporate hierarchy. References the account that is owned or controlled by the parent account. Enables downward traversal for subsidiary-level analysis.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Account Hierarchy; COPAS Joint Interest Billing Standards

description: Identifier of the parent account in the corporate hierarchy. References the account that owns or controls the child account. Used to traverse upward in the hierarchy tree for consolidated credit exposure and group-level reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Account Hierarchy; COPAS Joint Interest Billing Standards

description: Identifier of the topmost entity in the corporate ownership chain (e.g., the ultimate holding company of an IOC or NOC group). Used for consolidated credit exposure calculations, group-level risk management, and enterprise-wide commercial relationship reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AR Credit Management; IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements

description: Date on which the account hierarchy relationship record was formally approved by authorized personnel. Supports SOX audit trail requirements and master data governance processes.
reference: SOX Section 302/404 Internal Controls; SAP S/4HANA Workflow

description: Name or user identifier of the authorized personnel who approved this account hierarchy relationship record. Required for SOX audit trail and segregation of duties compliance in financial and commercial master data management.
reference: SOX Section 302/404 Internal Controls; SAP S/4HANA Authorization Management

description: Indicates whether the child account is included in the parent's consolidated financial statements (True) or treated as an equity-method investment or excluded entity (False). Drives financial consolidation logic in SAP FI and group-level credit exposure calculations per IFRS 10 and GAAP.
reference: IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements; GAAP ASC 810; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

description: Business classification of the child account entity type within the oil and gas commercial ecosystem. 'ioc' = International Oil Company (IOC); 'noc' = National Oil Company (NOC); 'refiner' = petroleum refiner; 'trader' = commodity trading house; 'industrial' = industrial consumer; 'distributor' = wholesale distributor; 'retail' = downstream retail operator; 'government' = government or state entity. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ioc|noc|refiner|trader|industrial|distributor|retail|government — promote to reference product]
reference: API Industry Classification; OPEC Member Classification; SAP S/4HANA SD Customer Classification

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction in which the child entity is legally incorporated or registered (e.g., USA, GBR, SAU, NLD). Critical for regulatory compliance, sanctions screening, Know Your Customer (KYC) due diligence, and cross-border tax reporting.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; FATF KYC/AML Standards; SEC Regulation S-X; OFAC Sanctions Compliance

description: Timestamp when this account hierarchy relationship record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and SOX compliance requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: SOX Section 302/404 Audit Trail; SAP S/4HANA Change Document; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards

description: Indicates whether the child account's credit exposure is aggregated into the parent's consolidated credit limit for group-level credit risk management (True) or managed independently (False). Supports enterprise-wide credit risk management for multinational IOC, NOC, and trading house groups.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AR Credit Management; COPAS Joint Interest Billing (JIB) Standards

description: Maximum approved credit exposure limit in US Dollars (USD) for the child account within this hierarchy relationship. Used for consolidated credit risk management, group-level credit exposure monitoring, and credit approval workflows in oil and gas wholesale trading and supply operations.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AR Credit Management; COPAS Joint Interest Billing (JIB) Standards; IFRS 9 Financial Instruments

description: External credit rating assigned to the child account entity by a recognized credit rating agency (e.g., S&P: AAA, AA+, BBB-; Moody's: Aaa, Aa1, Baa3; Fitch: AAA, AA+, BBB-) or an internal credit scoring grade. Used for credit risk assessment, payment terms determination, and counterparty risk management in oil and gas commercial operations.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AR Credit Management; IFRS 9 Financial Instruments; S&P/Moody's/Fitch Rating Scales

description: Name or code of the agency that issued the credit rating for the child account entity. 'SP' = Standard and Poor's; 'Moodys' = Moody's Investors Service; 'Fitch' = Fitch Ratings; 'internal' = Oil Gas internal credit scoring model; 'DBRS' = DBRS Morningstar.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AR Credit Management; IFRS 9 Financial Instruments; SEC Credit Rating Agency Regulations

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this account hierarchy record originated. 'SAP_SD' = SAP S/4HANA Sales and Distribution customer hierarchy; 'SAP_FI' = SAP S/4HANA Financial Accounting credit management; 'SAP_JVA' = SAP Joint Venture Accounting; 'Quorum' = Quorum Land System; 'manual' = manually entered; 'legacy' = migrated from legacy system.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD/FI/JVA Modules; Quorum Land System; Databricks Lakehouse Data Lineage Standards

description: Nine-digit Dun and Bradstreet (D&B) Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number uniquely identifying the child entity in the global business registry. Used for credit risk assessment, supplier qualification, and Know Your Customer (KYC) verification in oil and gas procurement and commercial operations.
reference: Dun and Bradstreet DUNS Standard; COPAS Vendor Qualification; API Supplier Standards

description: The date from which this parent-child hierarchy relationship becomes valid and binding. Used for time-slice queries to determine the correct hierarchy structure at any point in time, supporting historical reporting and audit requirements.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Customer Hierarchy; IFRS 10; SOX Audit Requirements

description: The date on which this parent-child hierarchy relationship ceases to be valid. Null indicates an open-ended, currently active relationship. Supports temporal hierarchy management for corporate restructurings, mergers, acquisitions, and divestments common in the oil and gas industry.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Customer Hierarchy; IFRS 10; SOX Audit Requirements

description: Workflow approval status for the account hierarchy relationship record. 'draft' = initial creation not yet submitted; 'submitted' = submitted for approval; 'approved' = approved by authorized personnel; 'rejected' = rejected and requires revision; 'under_review' = under compliance or legal review. Supports SOX internal controls and segregation of duties requirements.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Workflow; SOX Internal Controls; COPAS Accounting Standards

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this hierarchy relationship record within the enterprise. Aligns with SAP account hierarchy node codes used in SD and FI modules for group-level billing and credit management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Customer Hierarchy; ISO 6523 Organisation Identifier

description: Numeric depth level of the child account within the corporate hierarchy tree, where level 1 represents the ultimate parent entity. Used for hierarchical rollup queries, consolidated reporting, and credit exposure aggregation across multinational IOC and NOC group structures.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Customer Hierarchy; IFRS 10

description: Human-readable descriptive name for the hierarchy relationship or hierarchy group (e.g., 'Shell Group — EMEA Downstream', 'Saudi Aramco Trading Affiliates'). Supports business user identification and reporting labels.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Customer Hierarchy

description: Materialized path string representing the full ancestry chain from ultimate parent to the current child node (e.g., '/10001/10045/10312'). Enables efficient subtree queries and hierarchy traversal without recursive joins in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Best Practices

description: Current lifecycle status of the account hierarchy relationship. 'active' = currently valid and in use; 'inactive' = temporarily not in use; 'pending' = awaiting approval or activation; 'terminated' = permanently ended; 'suspended' = temporarily suspended pending review or compliance action.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module; COPAS Accounting Standards

description: Classification of the hierarchy relationship purpose. 'corporate' = legal ownership structure; 'commercial' = commercial/trading group; 'credit' = credit consolidation group; 'operational' = operational reporting rollup; 'jv_partner' = Joint Venture (JV) partner group structure used in Production Sharing Agreement (PSA) and Joint Operating Agreement (JOA) management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD/FI Module; COPAS Joint Interest Billing (JIB) Standards

description: Oil and gas industry value chain segment in which the child account primarily operates. 'upstream' = Exploration and Production (E&P); 'midstream' = transportation and storage; 'downstream' = refining and marketing; 'petrochemical' = petrochemical manufacturing; 'integrated' = vertically integrated operations; 'services' = oilfield services and equipment.
reference: API Industry Segment Classification; SPE PRMS Framework; SAP S/4HANA Industry Solution for Oil and Gas

description: Reference number of the Joint Operating Agreement (JOA) or Production Sharing Agreement (PSA) governing the relationship between parent and child accounts in joint venture structures. Links the hierarchy record to the contractual framework for Working Interest (WI) and Net Revenue Interest (NRI) management.
reference: COPAS Joint Interest Billing (JIB) Standards; SAP Joint Venture Accounting Module; API JOA Standards; BOEM Offshore Lease Requirements

description: Date on which the most recent Know Your Customer (KYC) compliance review was completed for the child account entity. Used to track KYC renewal cycles and ensure compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) and sanctions screening requirements.
reference: FATF KYC/AML Recommendations; OFAC Sanctions Compliance; SOX Internal Controls

description: Current Know Your Customer (KYC) compliance verification status for the child account entity. 'approved' = KYC checks passed and entity cleared for trading; 'pending' = initial KYC submission awaiting review; 'under_review' = KYC documentation under compliance review; 'rejected' = KYC failed, entity blocked from trading; 'expired' = KYC approval has lapsed and requires renewal.
reference: FATF KYC/AML Recommendations; OFAC Sanctions Compliance; Enablon HSE Management Compliance Module; SOX Internal Controls

description: Timestamp when this account hierarchy relationship record was most recently modified. Used for incremental data loading, change data capture (CDC), and audit trail maintenance in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: SOX Section 302/404 Audit Trail; SAP S/4HANA Change Document; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards

description: 20-character ISO 17442 Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) code assigned to the child entity by a globally recognized LEI issuer. Mandatory for financial market participants under EMIR and Dodd-Frank reporting. Used for unambiguous entity identification in cross-border oil and gas trading and derivatives transactions.
reference: ISO 17442 Legal Entity Identifier (LEI); EMIR Reporting Requirements; Dodd-Frank Act; FERC Reporting

description: Free-text field for capturing additional business context, special conditions, or commentary related to the account hierarchy relationship (e.g., notes on corporate restructuring, merger/acquisition context, regulatory restrictions, or special commercial arrangements).
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module; COPAS Accounting Standards

description: Percentage of equity ownership held by the parent account in the child account (0.0000 to 100.0000). Critical for determining consolidation thresholds under IFRS 10, calculating proportionate credit exposure, and managing Working Interest (WI) and Net Revenue Interest (NRI) allocations in joint venture structures.
reference: IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements; SEC Regulation S-X; COPAS Working Interest (WI) Standards

description: SAP payment terms code defining the standard payment conditions applicable to this hierarchy relationship (e.g., 'NT30' = Net 30 days, 'NT60' = Net 60 days, 'CIA' = Cash in Advance). Drives accounts receivable aging, cash flow forecasting, and Joint Interest Billing (JIB) settlement terms.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AR Payment Terms; COPAS Joint Interest Billing (JIB) Standards; IFRS/GAAP Revenue Recognition

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the primary transactional currency of this hierarchy relationship (e.g., USD for West Texas Intermediate (WTI) denominated contracts, EUR for European downstream operations). Used for consolidated credit exposure calculations and group-level financial reporting.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IFRS/GAAP Oil and Gas Accounting Standards

description: Describes the nature of the parent-child relationship between the two accounts. 'parent_subsidiary' = majority-owned subsidiary; 'holding_affiliate' = holding company to affiliate; 'branch_office' = legal branch of parent entity; 'trading_affiliate' = trading house affiliate; 'jv_partner' = Joint Venture (JV) partner relationship; 'retail_franchise' = downstream retail franchise network. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: parent_subsidiary|holding_affiliate|branch_office|trading_affiliate|jv_partner|retail_franchise — promote to reference product]
reference: IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements; SAP S/4HANA SD Customer Hierarchy; JOA/PSA Industry Standards

description: Indicates whether the child account entity has been screened against applicable sanctions lists (OFAC SDN, EU Consolidated List, UN Sanctions) as part of the KYC and counterparty onboarding process (True = screened and cleared; False = not yet screened or screening failed).
reference: OFAC Sanctions Compliance; EU Consolidated Sanctions List; UN Security Council Sanctions; FATF AML Standards

description: Natural key or identifier of this hierarchy relationship record in the originating operational system of record (e.g., SAP customer hierarchy node ID, Quorum land system record ID). Enables traceability and reconciliation between the Databricks Silver Layer and source systems.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module; Databricks Lakehouse Data Lineage Standards; SOX Audit Trail Requirements

description: Government-issued Tax Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) for the child entity. Required for Joint Interest Billing (JIB), royalty reporting, and regulatory tax filings. Sensitive business-confidential identifier subject to data protection controls.
reference: IRS EIN Requirements; COPAS Joint Interest Billing (JIB) Standards; SOX Financial Controls; IFRS/GAAP Tax Reporting

description: Percentage of voting rights held by the parent entity in the child entity. May differ from ownership percentage in cases of dual-class share structures or preference shares. Used for IFRS 10 control assessment and SEC disclosure requirements.
reference: IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements; SEC Regulation S-X; SOX Financial Controls

description: Working Interest (WI) percentage held by the child account entity in joint venture operations governed by this hierarchy relationship. Represents the proportionate share of costs and revenues in Exploration and Production (E&P) operations. Used in Joint Interest Billing (JIB) and Authorization for Expenditure (AFE) cost allocation.
reference: COPAS Working Interest (WI) Standards; SAP Joint Venture Accounting; SPE PRMS Framework; SEC Reserves Disclosure

description: Unique system-generated identifier for the customer complaint record. Primary key for the complaint data product within the customer domain.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Customer Service Notification

description: Foreign key linking to customer.account. Business justification: Complaints are often account-specific (not just counterparty-level). An account represents a specific commercial relationship, and complaints may be tied to that relationship rather than the counterpa
Reference to the commercial contract or sales agreement under which the disputed transaction or delivery occurred. Supports linkage to contract terms for resolution adjudication.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Sales Contract

description: Employee or team identifier of the primary resolution owner responsible for investigating and resolving the complaint. Drives workflow routing, SLA accountability, and workload reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Notification Responsible Person

description: Employee or senior manager identifier to whom the complaint has been escalated when SLA is breached or severity warrants senior intervention. Null when no escalation has occurred.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Notification Escalation; ISO 10002:2018

description: Foreign key linking to customer.contact. Business justification: Operational reality: complaints are filed by or involve specific contact persons. This link enables tracking who raised the complaint and facilitates follow-up communication.

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Complaint investigation, remediation, and settlement costs are allocated to operational cost centers (customer service, quality, HSE) for cost control and profitability analysis in oil & gas operation
Reference to the customer or counterparty (IOC, NOC, refiner, trader, wholesale buyer, industrial consumer, retail distributor) who raised the complaint. Links to the customer master record.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Business Partner

description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Settlement payments, credit notes, and warranty claims post to specific GL accounts (customer claims expense, sales returns). Required for accurate revenue recognition and expense matching.

Foreign key linking to venture.joa. Business justification: Quality or quantity complaints on JOA production require JOA dispute resolution procedures. Critical for JOA partner complaint tracking, crude quality dispute resolution, measurement discrepancy inves

Identifier of the JV partner or co-venturer involved in the complaint when jv_partner_involved is True. Links to the JV partner master record for notification and cost allocation under the Joint Interest Billing (JIB) process.
reference: SAP Joint Venture Accounting; JOA; COPAS

description: Foreign key linking to product.petroleum_product. Business justification: Complaints reference specific petroleum products with quality issues (off-spec sulfur, contamination, wrong grade delivered). Quality management and root cause analysis require linking complaints to p
Reference to the previous complaint record when repeat_complaint is True. Enables complaint lineage tracking and recurrence pattern analysis for continuous improvement and root cause elimination.

Foreign key linking to commercial.sales_order. Business justification: Complaints frequently reference specific sales orders for product quality, delivery, or invoicing issues. Required for root cause analysis, credit note processing, and customer satisfaction tracking l

Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Customer product quality complaints often trace to upstream vendor/supplier issues (contamination, off-spec material, blending errors). Business process: root cause analysis, vendor performance impact
Date on which the complaint was formally resolved and closed. Used to calculate resolution cycle time and SLA compliance. Null until complaint reaches resolved or closed status.
reference: ISO 10002:2018; SAP S/4HANA SD — Notification Completion Date

description: Final agreed financial settlement amount in US Dollars upon complaint resolution. May differ from claimed_amount_usd following negotiation or investigation. Triggers credit note issuance or payment adjustment in SAP FI.
reference: IFRS 15; COPAS; SAP S/4HANA FI — Credit Memo

description: Cargo or lifting reference number identifying the specific shipment, parcel, or delivery associated with the complaint. Links to cargo scheduling and vessel nomination records. Critical for short delivery, vessel delay, and product quality complaints.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Delivery Document; Avocet Production Operations — Cargo Allocation

description: Financial value of the customer's claim in US Dollars. Applicable to invoice disputes, pricing discrepancies, demurrage claims, and short delivery financial impacts. Used for credit risk assessment and financial provisioning under IFRS 15.
reference: IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers; COPAS; SAP S/4HANA FI

description: Volume quantity in barrels (BBL) that the customer claims was short-delivered, off-spec, or otherwise in dispute. Applicable primarily to short delivery and product quality complaints. Expressed in standard barrels at 60°F per API MPMS standards.
reference: API MPMS Chapter 11 — Physical Properties; API RP 2003

description: Channel through which the complaint was originally submitted by the customer. Telex is included as it remains in use for formal maritime and cargo communications in the oil and gas industry. Supports channel analytics and intake process optimization.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Notification Origin; ISO 10002:2018

description: Primary classification of the complaint type. Drives routing to the appropriate resolution team and root cause analysis framework. Categories align with oil and gas commercial operations: product_quality (off-spec crude/products), short_delivery (volume shortfall), invoice_dispute (billing error), vessel_delay (FPSO/tanker scheduling), documentation_error (bill of lading, COA), pricing_discrepancy (WTI/Brent differential disputes).
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Notification Type; API RP 2003; ISO 10002:2018

description: Calendar date on which the customer formally raised or submitted the complaint. Represents the principal business event date for SLA measurement and regulatory reporting purposes.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Notification Date

description: Detailed narrative description of the complaint as submitted by the customer. Captures the full context of the issue including specific parameters, quantities, dates, and circumstances. Classified confidential as it may contain commercially sensitive counterparty information.
reference: ISO 10002:2018; SAP S/4HANA SD — Notification Long Text

description: Current lifecycle state of the complaint workflow. Drives SLA monitoring, escalation triggers, and management reporting. 'pending_customer' indicates awaiting customer response; 'escalated' indicates breach of resolution SLA or senior management involvement.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Notification Status; ISO 10002:2018 Customer Satisfaction — Guidelines for Complaints Handling

description: Description of the corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) implemented to address the root cause and prevent recurrence. Supports continuous improvement tracking and regulatory compliance demonstration.
reference: ISO 10002:2018; ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management; API Q1/Q2

description: Date and time at which the complaint record was first created in the data platform (Silver Layer). Represents the audit trail creation timestamp, distinct from complaint_date (business event) and receipt_timestamp (system receipt). Supports data lineage and SOX audit compliance.
reference: SOX Section 404; NIST Cybersecurity Framework; SAP S/4HANA Audit Trail

description: SAP credit memo or credit note document number issued to the customer as part of the complaint resolution. Populated upon financial settlement for invoice disputes, pricing discrepancies, or short delivery claims. Links to SAP FI accounts receivable.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI — Credit Memo; IFRS 15; COPAS

description: Customer's expressed satisfaction level following complaint resolution. Captured via formal feedback mechanism or account manager assessment. Drives customer relationship health scoring and retention risk identification.
reference: ISO 10002:2018; ISO 10004:2018 Customer Satisfaction — Monitoring and Measuring

description: Numeric satisfaction rating provided by the customer following resolution, typically on a scale of 1 to 10. Complements the qualitative customer_satisfaction_outcome field. Used for KPI reporting and account health monitoring.

Outbound delivery or bill of lading number associated with the complaint. Distinct from cargo_reference in that it represents the logistics execution document rather than the commercial cargo nomination.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Outbound Delivery; PHMSA Pipeline Delivery Records

description: Indicates whether the complaint has been formally escalated to senior management or a specialist team. True when escalation_owner_id is populated and formal escalation process has been triggered.
reference: ISO 10002:2018; SAP S/4HANA SD — Notification Escalation

description: Reference number of the associated HSE incident record in Enablon HSE Management system, when the complaint has triggered a parallel safety or environmental incident investigation. Null when hse_related is False.
reference: Enablon HSE Management — Incident Reference; OSHA 29 CFR 1904

business_glossary_term: Health Safety and Environment (HSE) Related Flag
description: Indicates whether the complaint has an associated Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) implication, such as a product quality issue involving H2S content, NORM contamination, or a delivery incident with environmental impact. Triggers parallel HSE incident workflow in Enablon.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR; EPA 40 CFR; Enablon HSE Management; API RP 55

description: SAP billing document or invoice number relevant to the complaint, particularly for invoice dispute and pricing discrepancy categories. Enables direct linkage to financial records for credit note or adjustment processing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI — Billing Document; COPAS Accounting Procedures; IFRS 15

description: Indicates whether a Joint Venture (JV) partner or Production Sharing Agreement (PSA) co-venturer is implicated in the complaint, requiring notification and coordination under the Joint Operating Agreement (JOA). Triggers JV accounting and partner notification workflows.
reference: SAP Joint Venture Accounting — JV Partner; JOA Standard Terms; COPAS

description: Date and time of the most recent modification to the complaint record in the data platform. Used for incremental data loading, change data capture, and audit trail maintenance. Supports SOX compliance and data governance.
reference: SOX Section 404; NIST Cybersecurity Framework; Databricks Delta Lake Change Data Feed

description: Precise date and time at which the complaint was received and registered in the system. Used for SLA clock start and audit trail purposes. Distinct from complaint_date which captures the business event date.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Notification Creation Time

description: Externally communicated complaint reference number shared with the customer for tracking purposes. Follows the format COMP-YYYY-NNNNNN. Used in all customer-facing correspondence and SAP SD service notification references.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Service Notification Number

description: Name of the regulatory authority notified in connection with the complaint (e.g., EPA, BSEE, PHMSA, FERC). Populated only when regulatory_notification_required is True. Supports regulatory compliance audit trail.
reference: EPA; BSEE; PHMSA; FERC; Enablon HSE Management

description: Indicates whether the complaint involves a matter requiring notification to a regulatory body (e.g., EPA for environmental product quality issues, BSEE for offshore delivery failures, PHMSA for pipeline delivery incidents). Triggers compliance workflow in Enablon HSE Management.
reference: EPA 40 CFR; BSEE 30 CFR Part 250; PHMSA 49 CFR; Enablon HSE Management

description: Indicates whether this complaint represents a recurrence of a previously resolved complaint from the same customer for the same root cause or issue type. Signals ineffective corrective action and triggers enhanced investigation under continuous improvement protocols.
reference: ISO 10002:2018; ISO 9001:2015 Clause 10.2 — Nonconformity and Corrective Action

description: Detailed narrative of the actions taken to resolve the complaint, including investigation findings, corrective measures applied, and any commercial settlement agreed. Classified confidential due to commercially sensitive content.
reference: ISO 10002:2018; SAP S/4HANA SD — Notification Resolution Text

description: High-level classification of the identified root cause of the complaint. Supports systemic trend analysis and continuous improvement programs. process_failure: upstream or downstream process deviation; equipment_failure: metering, pumping, or vessel equipment; human_error: operational or administrative error; supplier_issue: third-party or JV partner failure; logistics_failure: transportation or scheduling failure; measurement_error: API MPMS measurement discrepancy.
reference: API RP 2003; ISO 10002:2018; Enablon HSE Management — Root Cause Analysis

description: Detailed narrative of the identified root cause following investigation. Provides specific technical or operational context beyond the root_cause_category classification. Used for corrective action planning and lessons learned documentation.
reference: ISO 10002:2018; API RP 2003; Enablon HSE Management

description: Business impact severity rating assigned at intake or triage. Critical: potential regulatory breach, HSE implication, or major commercial loss. High: significant financial impact or key account at risk. Medium: moderate operational impact. Low: minor administrative issue. Drives SLA target assignment and escalation thresholds.

Indicates whether the complaint resolution exceeded the target resolution date, constituting an SLA breach. True when actual_resolution_date exceeds target_resolution_date or when complaint remains open past target date. Drives management reporting and continuous improvement.

Original system identifier or notification number from the operational system of record (e.g., SAP SD service notification number, CRM case ID) from which this complaint record was sourced. Supports data lineage and reconciliation with upstream systems.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Service Notification; Data Governance — Lineage

description: Secondary classification providing granular detail within the complaint category. Examples include: off-spec sulfur content, density out-of-range, TAN exceedance, RON shortfall, volume meter discrepancy, demurrage claim, laytime dispute, letter of credit discrepancy. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: off_spec_sulfur|off_spec_density|off_spec_tan|off_spec_ron|volume_meter|demurrage|laytime|lc_discrepancy|other — promote to reference product]
reference: API MPMS (Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards); SAP S/4HANA SD

description: Contractually or operationally committed date by which the complaint must be resolved. Derived from complaint severity and SLA policy. Used for SLA breach monitoring and escalation triggering.
reference: ISO 10002:2018; SAP S/4HANA SD — Notification Required End Date

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the individual contact person record within the Oil Gas customer domain. Serves as the primary key for all downstream joins and relationship resolution.
reference: ISO/IEC 11179 Data Element Naming and Definition Standards

description: Reference to the parent counterparty or customer account (IOC, NOC, refiner, trader, industrial consumer) to which this contact belongs. Supports account hierarchy and relationship management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Business Partner Contact Assignment

description: Foreign key linking to customer.customer_counterparty. Business justification: Contacts can be associated directly with counterparties (not just through accounts). This supports scenarios where a contact represents the counterparty entity itself. The organization_name on contact

Maximum monetary value in US Dollars that this contact is authorized to approve for transactions, AFEs (Authorization for Expenditure), purchase orders, or contract amendments on behalf of their organization. Critical for COPAS AFE management and SOX financial controls.
reference: COPAS — Authorization for Expenditure (AFE) approval thresholds; SOX Section 302/404 financial authorization controls; SAP S/4HANA MM — Purchasing authorization limits

description: Name of the executive assistant or administrative contact who manages scheduling and correspondence on behalf of this contact. Used for executive-level relationship management with senior IOC, NOC, and industrial customer representatives.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Contact Person Assistant field; CRM relationship management best practices

description: Phone number for the executive assistant or administrative contact. Used to schedule meetings and route communications for senior counterparty representatives who delegate correspondence management.
reference: GDPR Article 4; ITU-T E.164; SAP S/4HANA SD — Assistant Phone field

description: Indicates the contractual and operational authority level of the contact: signatory (authorized to execute contracts/AFEs), approver (can approve transactions up to defined limits), operational (day-to-day operational decisions), informational (receives communications only). Critical for AFE authorization, JIB approvals, and contract execution workflows.
