description: The last date of the laycan window — the latest date by which the vessel must arrive and tender NOR. If the vessel arrives after this date, the charterer has the right to cancel the charter party.
reference: INCOTERMS 2020; Charterparty Standard Terms; BIMCO Voyage Charter Clauses

description: The first date of the laycan (laydays cancelling) window — the earliest date the vessel may arrive at the loading or discharge port and tender Notice of Readiness (NOR) under the charter party terms.
reference: INCOTERMS 2020; Charterparty Standard Terms; BIMCO Voyage Charter Clauses

description: The calendar month (YYYY-MM format) of the monthly lifting program to which this nomination belongs. Used to reconcile nominations against the monthly crude lifting schedule and production allocation.
reference: Avocet Production Operations; Oil Gas Monthly Lifting Program Procedures

description: The UN/LOCODE five-character code identifying the port or terminal from which the cargo is to be loaded onto the vessel. Applicable for FOB and similar delivery terms where Oil Gas is the seller at the load port.
reference: UN/LOCODE Port Code Standard; BIMCO Port Definitions

description: The quantity of product formally requested by the customer in the nomination. Expressed in the unit of measure specified by the volume_uom field (BBL, MT, or MMBTU depending on product type and contract terms).
reference: API MPMS Chapter 12 — Calculation of Petroleum Quantities; SPE PRMS

description: The calendar date on which the customer formally submitted the nomination request. Represents the principal business event date for the nomination lifecycle.
reference: Oil Gas Internal Nomination Procedures; Avocet Production Operations

description: Current workflow lifecycle state of the nomination. Tracks progression from initial customer submission through commercial confirmation, amendment, cancellation, or expiry without fulfillment.
reference: Oil Gas Internal Nomination Procedures; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

description: Classification of the nomination by commercial basis and delivery mode. Distinguishes between term contract liftings, spot sale cargoes, pipeline nominations, and product exchange arrangements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: term_contract|spot_sale|pipeline|cargo|exchange — promote to reference product]
reference: COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards; FERC Natural Gas Pipeline Regulations

description: For pipeline gas nominations, the NAESB/FERC nomination cycle in which this nomination was submitted (Timely, Evening, Intraday 1, 2, or 3). Null for marine cargo nominations.
reference: NAESB WGQ Business Practice Standards; FERC Order 587 — Gas Pipeline Nomination Standards

description: The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the price differential and any fixed price components are denominated (typically USD for international crude and LNG trades).
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IFRS 9 Financial Instruments

description: The contractual premium or discount (in USD per BBL or USD per MMBTU) applied to the benchmark pricing basis for this specific nomination. Reflects quality, location, and timing adjustments negotiated in the contract.
reference: COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards; IFRS 9 Financial Instruments

description: The benchmark price index against which the nominated cargo will be priced per the contract terms (e.g., Dated Brent, WTI Cushing, Platts Dubai, NYMEX Natural Gas). Drives price calculation at bill of lading date or delivery. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: dated_brent|wti_cushing|platts_dubai|argus_sour|nymex_ng|ice_brent — promote to reference product]
reference: Platts Price Assessment Methodology; Argus Media Pricing Standards; FERC Market Transparency Rules

description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to the nomination, used in communications with the customer, terminal operators, and logistics teams. Follows the NOM- prefix convention.
reference: Oil Gas Internal Nomination Procedures; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

description: The specific delivery date requested by the customer within the laycan window, or the target pipeline delivery date for non-vessel nominations. Used for scheduling and logistics planning.
reference: Oil Gas Internal Nomination Procedures; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

description: Indicates whether the customer, vessel, and destination country have been screened against OFAC, UN, EU, and UK sanctions lists prior to nomination confirmation. Must be True before confirmation_timestamp is populated.
reference: OFAC SDN List Compliance; UN Security Council Sanctions; EU Sanctions Regulations; UK OFSI Sanctions

description: The FERC-assigned or pipeline operator-assigned code identifying the shipper of record for pipeline nominations. Required for FERC-regulated interstate pipeline capacity scheduling and balancing.
reference: FERC Order 636 — Pipeline Restructuring; PHMSA Pipeline Safety Regulations

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this nomination record originated. Supports data lineage tracking in the Silver Layer lakehouse. SAP_SD for SAP Sales and Distribution, AVOCET for Avocet Production Operations, ETRM for Energy Trading and Risk Management system.
reference: Oil Gas Data Governance Policy; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards

description: The maximum allowable percentage above the nominated volume that may be delivered without requiring a separate nomination amendment. Expressed as a positive percentage (e.g., 5.00 for 5% over).
reference: INCOTERMS 2020; Standard Crude Oil Sale and Purchase Agreement Terms

description: The minimum allowable percentage below the nominated volume that the customer may accept at delivery without triggering a contract shortfall or take-or-pay obligation. Expressed as a negative percentage (e.g., -5.00 for 5% under).
reference: INCOTERMS 2020; Standard Crude Oil Sale and Purchase Agreement Terms

description: The date and time at which the nomination record was most recently modified. Updated on every status change, amendment, or data correction to support audit trail and change tracking requirements.
reference: SOX Section 302/404 — Internal Controls; Oil Gas Data Governance Policy

description: The name of the tanker or LNG carrier nominated by the customer or charterer to lift the cargo. Populated for marine cargo nominations; null for pipeline nominations.
reference: IMO Ship Identification Standards; BIMCO Vessel Nomination Clauses

description: The outcome of the vessel vetting process conducted against OCIMF SIRE or CDI inspection records. Approved vessels are cleared for loading; rejected vessels must be substituted; conditional approvals require additional review.
reference: OCIMF SIRE Programme; CDI Marine Inspection Standards; BSEE Offshore Safety Regulations

business_glossary_term: Volume in Barrels of Oil Equivalent (BOE)
description: Nominated volume converted to Barrels of Oil Equivalent (BOE) for cross-commodity comparison, portfolio reporting, and SEC reserves disclosure alignment. Conversion factors applied per API/SPE standards.
reference: API MPMS; SPE PRMS Reserves Classification; SEC Regulation S-X Rule 4-10

description: Unit of measure in which the nominated volume is expressed. BBL (barrels) for crude and liquid products, MT (metric tonnes) for LNG and bulk cargoes, MMBTU for natural gas, MCF/MMCF for pipeline gas volumes, M3 for metric volume reporting.
reference: API MPMS Chapter 11 — Physical Properties; FERC Gas Measurement Standards

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the offtake entitlement record. Primary key for this entity in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Entity role: MASTER_AGREEMENT — represents a contractual entitlement container defining a counterparty's right to lift volumes under a term offtake agreement or PSA lifting schedule.

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Offtake entitlements require ongoing administration by commercial analysts who track working interest calculations, equity share reconciliations, overlift/underlift positions, and cost recovery volume

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Entitlement administration, overlift/underlift reconciliation, and JV partner coordination costs are allocated to commercial/JV administration cost centers for overhead tracking and partner billing.
Reference to the customer or counterparty (IOC, NOC, refiner, trader, or wholesale buyer) holding this offtake entitlement. Identifies the lifting party in the JOA or PSA partner lifting schedule.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module; COPAS JIB Standards

description: Foreign key linking to customer.delivery_point. Business justification: Offtake entitlement delivery_point string should be a FK reference to the delivery_point master table. This enables proper referential integrity and allows joining to get full delivery point details.
Reference to the producing field or asset from which the entitled volumes are to be lifted. Associates the entitlement with the specific upstream production source.

Foreign key linking to venture.joa. Business justification: Offtake entitlements derive from JOA working interest and net revenue interest allocations. Critical for JOA-based entitlement calculation, equity production allocation, partner balancing, and overlif

Reference to the parent term offtake agreement, Joint Operating Agreement (JOA), or Production Sharing Agreement (PSA) under which this entitlement is granted. Links the entitlement to its governing commercial contract.

Foreign key linking to product.petroleum_product. Business justification: Offtake entitlements specify which petroleum product the customer is entitled to lift under PSC/JOA agreements. Essential for equity crude allocation, gas balancing, and revenue distribution calculati

Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Equity production entitlements (working interest, net revenue interest) are allocated to field-level profit centers for upstream accounting, reserve booking, and field economics. Core upstream financi

Foreign key linking to venture.psa. Business justification: PSA profit oil and cost recovery volumes establish contractor offtake entitlements. Essential for PSA entitlement determination, cost recovery ceiling tracking, profit oil split calculation, and contr

Foreign key linking to reservoir.reservoir. Business justification: In PSC/JOA arrangements with reservoir-specific cost recovery pools (e.g., separate accounting for deepwater vs shallow reservoirs in same field), offtake entitlements are calculated and tracked at re

Authorization for Expenditure (AFE) number associated with the capital or operating program linked to this entitlement period. Used for JIB cost allocation and partner billing reconciliation in SAP Joint Venture Accounting.
reference: SAP Joint Venture Accounting; COPAS Model Form Accounting Procedure; AFE Industry Standard

description: Classification of the governing commercial agreement type under which this entitlement is established. Determines the applicable accounting treatment, partner balancing rules, and regulatory reporting obligations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PSA|JOA|term_offtake|spot|GSA|LNG_SPA|FPSO_offtake — promote to reference product]
reference: SPE-PRMS; COPAS; IFRS 15; SEC Regulation S-X Rule 4-10

description: Method used to resolve overlift/underlift imbalances between JOA partners at period end. Cash settlement involves monetary payment; in-kind involves physical volume make-up; carry-forward defers the imbalance to the next period; deemed-sold treats the imbalance as a notional sale.
reference: COPAS Model Form Accounting Procedure; SAP Joint Venture Accounting; IFRS 15

description: Type of financial security instrument required from the customer to support credit exposure under this entitlement. Determined by credit rating and exposure level. Letter of credit and bank guarantees are standard instruments in international crude oil and LNG trading.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI; UCP 600 (ICC); IFRS 9; Basel III

description: Volume of cost oil or cost gas allocated to the contractor party for recovery of capital and operating expenditures under a Production Sharing Agreement (PSA). Expressed in the entitlement unit of measure. Applicable only to PSA-governed entitlements.
reference: PSA Industry Standard; SPE-PRMS; IFRS 6; COPAS

description: Timestamp when this offtake entitlement record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides the audit trail creation anchor for SOX compliance and data lineage tracking.

Maximum credit exposure approved for this customer under this offtake entitlement, expressed in the transaction currency. Enforced during cargo nomination and lifting authorization workflows to manage counterparty credit risk.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AR; COPAS; IFRS 9 Credit Risk; Basel III

description: External or internal credit rating assigned to the customer counterparty (e.g., S&P: AAA, AA+, BBB-; Moody's: Aaa, Baa1; or internal rating code). Used in credit risk assessment and determination of collateral or letter of credit requirements for lifting authorization.
reference: S&P Global Ratings; Moody's; Fitch; IFRS 9; Basel III; SAP S/4HANA FI

description: Total volume actually lifted by the customer against this entitlement from the period start date through the most recent reconciliation date. Expressed in the entitlement unit of measure. Used to compute remaining entitlement and overlift/underlift position.

ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which monetary values (entitlement value, overlift/underlift value, settlement amounts) are denominated. Typically USD for international crude and LNG transactions.
Mode of transportation used to deliver lifted volumes from the production source to the delivery point. Determines applicable logistics, demurrage, and PHMSA/FERC regulatory requirements.

Total contractual volume the customer is entitled to lift during the entitlement period, expressed in the designated unit of measure (BBL, MT, or MMBTU). Represents the gross entitlement before any adjustments for overlift/underlift carry-forward.
reference: SPE-PRMS; PSA/JOA Industry Standard; COPAS Model Form

description: Externally-known business identifier for this offtake entitlement record, typically assigned by the operator or JV administrator. Used in JIB statements, lifting schedules, and partner correspondence. Aligns with SAP JVA document numbering conventions.
reference: SAP Joint Venture Accounting; COPAS Model Form Accounting Procedure

description: The last calendar date of the entitlement period. Nullable for open-ended or evergreen offtake arrangements. Defines the closing boundary of the lifting window. Used in overlift/underlift position calculations and period-end reconciliation.

The first calendar date of the entitlement period during which the customer is contractually authorized to lift volumes. Defines the opening boundary of the lifting window under the term offtake agreement or PSA schedule.

Current lifecycle state of the offtake entitlement. Drives operational eligibility for scheduling lifts and triggers credit/compliance checks. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|suspended|terminated|pending|expired|cancelled — promote to reference product if additional states are required]

The customer's equity entitlement percentage, which may differ from Working Interest (WI) due to PSA cost recovery provisions, carried interest arrangements, or government back-in rights. Used in PSA lifting schedule calculations to determine the contractor's equity oil/gas share.
reference: PSA Industry Standard; SPE-PRMS; IFRS 6; SEC Regulation S-X Rule 4-10

description: Maximum allowable overlift or underlift volume before formal balancing or cash settlement is triggered. Expressed in the entitlement unit of measure. Contractually defined in the JOA or offtake agreement to accommodate operational variability in cargo sizes.
reference: COPAS Model Form Accounting Procedure; JOA Industry Standard

description: International Commercial Terms (Incoterms 2020) code defining the allocation of costs, risks, and responsibilities between seller and buyer for the delivery of lifted volumes. Governs title transfer, insurance obligations, and freight cost allocation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FOB|CIF|CFR|DES|DAP|FCA|EXW|DDP|CPT|CIP — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: Incoterms 2020 (ICC); COPAS; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

description: Joint Interest Billing (JIB) code used to allocate costs and revenues to the correct partner account in the joint venture accounting system. Enables accurate partner billing and cost recovery tracking in SAP Joint Venture Accounting per COPAS standards.
reference: SAP Joint Venture Accounting; COPAS Model Form Accounting Procedure

description: Indicates whether the customer has completed Know Your Customer (KYC) due diligence verification as required for counterparty onboarding under anti-money laundering (AML) and sanctions compliance programs. Must be True before entitlement activation.
reference: FATF Recommendations; FinCEN AML Rules; OFAC Sanctions; SOX

description: The most recent date on which the cumulative lifted volume, remaining entitlement, and overlift/underlift position were formally reconciled against production allocation records. Used to determine the currency of the entitlement position data.
reference: COPAS; Avocet Production Operations; SAP Joint Venture Accounting

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this offtake entitlement record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change tracking, audit compliance, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.

Classification of the lifting schedule cadence governing when the customer may nominate and execute lifts against this entitlement. Drives operational planning in Avocet Production Operations and cargo scheduling systems.
reference: Avocet Production Operations; JOA/PSA Industry Standard; COPAS

description: The Net Revenue Interest (NRI) percentage representing the customer's share of production revenue after deducting royalties, overriding royalty interests (ORRI), and other burdens. Distinct from WI as it reflects the net economic interest after all encumbrances.
reference: COPAS; Quorum Land System; SEC Regulation S-X Rule 4-10; SPE-PRMS

description: Number of calendar days prior to the scheduled lifting date by which the customer must submit a formal volume nomination. Contractually defined in the offtake agreement and used to trigger operational readiness workflows.
reference: JOA/PSA Industry Standard; Avocet Production Operations

description: Monetary value of the overlift or underlift position, calculated by applying the applicable pricing formula to the overlift/underlift volume. Used for cash settlement or in-kind balancing between JOA partners. Expressed in the transaction currency.
reference: COPAS Model Form Accounting Procedure; SAP Joint Venture Accounting; IFRS 15

description: Net overlift (positive) or underlift (negative) position of the customer relative to their entitlement as of the last reconciliation date. Expressed in the entitlement unit of measure. A positive value indicates the customer has lifted more than their entitlement (overlift); negative indicates underlift. Critical for JOA partner balancing and cash settlement calculations.
reference: COPAS Model Form Accounting Procedure; SAP Joint Venture Accounting; SPE-PRMS

description: Contractual payment terms governing settlement of invoices for lifted volumes (e.g., Net 30 days from Bill of Lading date, prepayment, letter of credit at sight). Defined in the offtake agreement and enforced in SAP S/4HANA SD billing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module; COPAS; IFRS 15; Incoterms 2020

description: Quality or location differential applied to the benchmark price to arrive at the actual transaction price for lifted volumes. Expressed in the transaction currency per unit of measure (e.g., USD/BBL). May be positive (premium) or negative (discount) relative to the benchmark.
reference: API MPMS; COPAS; Platts; Argus Media

description: The benchmark or pricing formula basis used to value lifted volumes under this entitlement (e.g., WTI, Brent, Dubai Fateh, Henry Hub for gas, JKM for LNG). Determines the reference price index applied in overlift/underlift cash settlement calculations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WTI|Brent|Dubai|ANSI|Henry_Hub|JKM|NBP|formula|Platts_dated — promote to reference product]
reference: FERC; Platts; Argus Media; COPAS; IFRS 9

description: Volume of profit oil or profit gas allocated to the contractor party after cost recovery under a Production Sharing Agreement (PSA). Represents the contractor's share of production above the cost recovery tranche, split per the PSA profit-sharing formula.

Residual volume the customer is still entitled to lift within the current entitlement period, calculated as entitled volume minus cumulative lifted volume. Stored as a business-tracked field updated at each reconciliation cycle rather than computed on-the-fly, supporting operational scheduling decisions.

The applicable royalty rate percentage deducted from gross production entitlement before computing the customer's net lifting volume. Includes government royalties, lessor royalties, and overriding royalty interests (ORRI) as applicable under the governing lease or PSA.
reference: BOEM; BSEE; Quorum Land System; COPAS; ONRR Reporting Requirements

description: Indicates whether the customer and associated entities have been screened against applicable sanctions lists (OFAC SDN, EU Consolidated List, UN Sanctions) as part of the counterparty compliance process. Required for regulatory compliance in international crude and LNG trading.
reference: OFAC; EU Sanctions Regulation; UN Security Council Resolutions; SOX

description: Standard unit in which entitlement volumes are expressed and tracked. BBL (barrels) for crude oil and condensate, MT (metric tonnes) for LNG/LPG, MMBTU for gas, MCF/MMCF for gas volumes. Governs all volume calculations within this entitlement record.

The customer's Working Interest (WI) percentage in the joint venture or production sharing agreement, expressed as a decimal fraction (e.g., 0.250000 = 25%). Drives the proportional entitlement calculation from gross field production.
reference: SPE-PRMS; JOA Industry Standard; COPAS; SEC Regulation S-X Rule 4-10

description: Unique identifier for the bank detail record. Primary key for customer banking and settlement instruction records.
Reference to the specific customer account associated with this banking instruction. Supports multiple bank details per customer account for different currencies or payment types.

Reference to the customer or counterparty associated with this bank detail record. Links to the customer master data for IOCs, NOCs, refiners, traders, wholesale buyers, industrial consumers, and retail distributors.
Reference to the employee who approved this bank detail record. Required for segregation of duties and audit trail in financial controls per SOX compliance requirements.
Self-referencing FK on bank_detail (previous_bank_detail_id)
Legal name of the beneficiary account holder as registered with the bank. Must match KYC records and contract counterparty legal name for compliance and payment processing.

Status of internal approval workflow for this bank detail record. Approved records are eligible for payment processing; pending approval requires management review; rejected records are blocked; under review indicates compliance investigation.
Date and time when this bank detail record was approved for payment processing. Required for audit trail and compliance documentation.
City location of the beneficiary bank branch. Used for payment routing and correspondent bank identification in international settlements.
Primary address line of the beneficiary bank branch. Required for wire transfer instructions and correspondent banking relationships.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the bank location. Critical for sanctions compliance, correspondent banking relationships, and regulatory reporting in cross-border petroleum transactions.

Current lifecycle status of the bank detail record. Active records are eligible for payment processing; pending verification requires compliance review; suspended records are temporarily blocked; expired records require renewal.

Classification of the banking instruction by purpose and payment method. Primary is the default settlement account; alternate provides backup routing; escrow supports joint venture and production sharing agreement settlements; letter of credit for trade finance.
Full legal name of the beneficiary bank institution. Required for wire transfer execution and accounts receivable settlement across international crude oil, LNG, and refined product transactions.
City of the beneficiary address. Required for payment routing and compliance screening in international crude oil and LNG settlements.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the beneficiary address. Used for sanctions screening, jurisdiction risk assessment, and regulatory reporting in international petroleum transactions.
Primary address line for the beneficiary. Required for international wire transfer compliance and anti-money laundering verification in cross-border petroleum transactions.
Name of the ultimate beneficiary receiving the payment. May differ from account holder name in cases of third-party payment arrangements or joint venture settlements.
Date and time when this bank detail record was first created in the system. Required for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for this bank account. Supports multi-currency settlement requirements for international crude oil, LNG, and refined product transactions denominated in USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, and other currencies.
Date from which this bank detail record becomes active and eligible for payment processing. Supports time-bound banking instructions and planned account transitions.
Date until which this bank detail record remains valid. Nullable for open-ended banking instructions. Used for temporary accounts, escrow arrangements, and time-limited joint venture settlements.

International Bank Account Number for beneficiary account identification in SEPA and international markets. Used primarily for European and Middle Eastern counterparties in petroleum product settlements.
Account number at the intermediary bank for routing the payment. Required for correspondent banking chains in international crude oil and LNG settlements.
Name of the intermediary or correspondent bank used for routing international payments. Required when direct correspondent banking relationship does not exist between payer and beneficiary banks.

business_glossary_term: Intermediary Bank Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT) Business Identifier Code (BIC)
description: SWIFT BIC code for the intermediary bank. Used for multi-hop international wire transfers in complex cross-border petroleum transactions.

Flag indicating whether the bank detail has been validated against KYC records and beneficial ownership documentation. Required for anti-money laundering compliance in international petroleum transactions.

Free-text field for additional payment instructions, special handling requirements, or compliance notes. Used for documenting joint venture partner splits, letter of credit references, or regulatory reporting requirements.

Additional payment reference or remittance information to be included in wire transfer instructions. Used for invoice reconciliation and joint venture partner identification in petroleum transactions.

Preferred payment network or clearing system for settlement execution. SWIFT for international wire transfers, ACH for US domestic batch payments, SEPA for European transfers, Fedwire and CHIPS for US real-time gross settlement, TARGET2 for European central bank settlements, RTGS for real-time gross settlement in various jurisdictions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: swift|ach|sepa|fedwire|chips|target2|rtgs — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

Numeric ranking indicating the priority order for payment processing when multiple bank details exist for the same customer account. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used for automatic payment routing in accounts receivable settlement.
External business identifier for this bank detail record. Used for cross-system reconciliation and customer communication regarding payment instructions.
Nine-digit ABA routing transit number for US domestic wire transfers and ACH payments. Used for domestic crude oil and refined product settlements with US-based counterparties.
reference: American Bankers Association (ABA) Routing Number Standard

description: Flag indicating whether the bank and beneficiary have been screened against OFAC SDN, EU Consolidated, UN Security Council, and HM Treasury sanctions lists. Required before processing any payment in crude oil, LNG, or refined product transactions.
Date of the most recent sanctions screening for this bank detail record. Must be current within regulatory requirements before payment execution.
Six-digit bank sort code for UK domestic payments. Used for settlements with UK-based refiners, traders, and wholesale buyers in the petroleum sector.
reference: UK Payments Administration Sort Code Standard

business_glossary_term: Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT) Business Identifier Code (BIC)
description: SWIFT BIC code identifying the beneficiary bank for international wire transfers. Eight or eleven character code used for cross-border payment routing in crude oil, LNG, and refined product transactions.
Date and time when this bank detail record was last modified. Required for audit trail and change tracking in financial master data.
Date when the bank detail record was last verified through test transaction, bank confirmation letter, or third-party validation service. Required for audit trail and compliance documentation.

Method used to verify the bank account details. Test transaction sends small amount for confirmation; bank letter requires official bank documentation; third-party service uses external validation providers; customer declaration relies on signed attestation.

Status of bank detail verification process. Verified indicates successful validation of account ownership and routing information; pending indicates awaiting compliance review; failed indicates validation errors; expired indicates reverification required.
Unique surrogate identifier for each counterparty JOA commercial participation record

business_glossary_term: Counterparty Joa Participation - Customer Counterparty Id
description: Foreign key linking to the customer counterparty participating in the JOA commercial arrangement
Foreign key linking to the Joint Operating Agreement under which the commercial participation is governed

Current lifecycle status of the counterparty's commercial participation in the JOA. ACTIVE indicates ongoing commercial activity; SUSPENDED indicates temporary halt; TERMINATED indicates relationship ended; PENDING_APPROVAL indicates awaiting JOA partner approval
External reference number or identifier for the commercial contract or agreement that governs this counterparty's participation in the JOA

Indicates whether the counterparty has elected to take equity offtake (in-kind production allocation) under the JOA rather than cash settlement. True indicates physical offtake; false indicates cash or no offtake election
The volume of production in barrels that the counterparty is entitled to offtake under this JOA commercial arrangement, if applicable. Null for non-offtake roles
The date on which the counterparty's commercial participation in the JOA became effective, marking the start of offtake rights or supply obligations
The date on which the counterparty's commercial participation in the JOA ended or is scheduled to end, if applicable. Null indicates ongoing participation

The pricing benchmark or mechanism preferred by the counterparty for commercial transactions under this JOA. BRENT, WTI, DUBAI are crude benchmarks; PLATTS and ARGUS are pricing services; FIXED indicates fixed price; FORMULA indicates custom pricing formula

Categorical classification of the counterparty's commercial role in relation to the JOA. OFFTAKER indicates the counterparty purchases production; SUPPLIER provides goods or services; MARKETING_AGENT handles sales; REFINING_PARTNER processes crude; TRANSPORTATION_PROVIDER handles logistics
Unique surrogate identifier for each customer price index preference record. Primary key for the price_index_preference data product in the customer domain.
reference: COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

description: Foreign key linking to customer.account. Business justification: Pricing preferences can be account-specific. Different accounts under the same counterparty may have different pricing terms, indices, and formulas based on their specific commercial agreements.

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pricing formulas and index preferences require commercial manager approval before contract execution. Regulatory requirement in many jurisdictions for price risk management. approved_by is denormalize
Reference to the commercial contract or sales agreement under which this pricing index preference applies. Supports back-office settlement and deal structuring.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module; FERC Regulations; COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards

description: Reference to the customer account for which this price index preference is configured. Links to the customer master record in the SSOT customer domain.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module; COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards

description: Foreign key linking to venture.joa. Business justification: JOA partners may elect specific pricing bases for their equity crude offtake. Enables JOA partner-specific pricing elections, equity crude pricing administration, and partner commercial terms manageme

Foreign key linking to product.petroleum_product. Business justification: Price index preferences specify pricing formulas for specific petroleum products (crude grades, refined products, NGLs). Commercial teams configure product-specific pricing differentials and indices f

The commercial approval workflow status for this pricing index preference. 'draft' indicates under preparation; 'pending_approval' indicates submitted for commercial review; 'approved' indicates authorized for use in contracts; 'rejected' indicates not approved; 'withdrawn' indicates recalled by the submitter.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module; SOX Financial Controls; COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards

description: The date and time at which this pricing index preference was formally approved by the authorized commercial manager. Supports audit trail, SOX compliance, and contract lifecycle management.
reference: SOX Financial Controls; SAP S/4HANA SD Module; COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards

description: The maximum price per unit (in the differential_unit currency) above which the effective price will not rise, regardless of the benchmark index movement. Provides price protection for the buyer in volatile market conditions. Expressed in the same unit as differential_usd.
reference: COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards; IFRS 9 Financial Instruments; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

description: The date and time at which this price index preference record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance reporting in the Databricks Silver Layer lakehouse.
reference: SOX Financial Controls; NIST Cybersecurity Framework; COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards; GDPR Article 5

description: The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the price index and differential are denominated. Typically USD for international crude oil and products trading. Supports multi-currency commercial agreements and financial settlement.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IFRS 9 Financial Instruments; COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards; FERC Regulations

description: The standardized code identifying the delivery point or terminal associated with this pricing preference (e.g., Cushing OK for WTI, Rotterdam for Brent products). Aligns the pricing basis with the physical delivery location for FOB/CIF/DES pricing.
reference: API Standards; FERC Regulations; PHMSA Pipeline Safety Regulations; BOEM Offshore Leasing Regulations

description: The unit of measure for the pricing differential. USD per barrel (USD/BBL) for crude oil and liquid products; USD per MMBTU for natural gas and LNG; USD per metric ton (USD/MT) for petrochemicals; USD per thousand cubic feet (USD/MCF) or USD per gigajoule (USD/GJ) for gas contracts.
reference: API Standards; FERC Regulations; COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards; ISO 80000 Quantities and Units

description: The premium or discount applied to the benchmark price index, expressed in USD per barrel (BBL) for crude oil and refined products, or USD per MMBTU for natural gas. A positive value indicates a premium above the index; a negative value indicates a discount below the index. Critical for commercial deal structuring and back-office settlement.
reference: COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards; API Standards; FERC Regulations; IFRS 9 Financial Instruments

description: The date from which this price index preference becomes effective and applicable to commercial transactions with the customer. Used to manage temporal validity of pricing configurations and support contract lifecycle management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module; COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards; IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers

description: The date on which this price index preference expires and is no longer applicable. Nullable for open-ended preferences. Supports contract pricing configuration and temporal validity management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module; COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards; IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers

description: The date as of which the delivered_volume_to_date, shortfall_volume, makeup_volume_available, and accrued_shortfall_penalty_amount figures were last calculated and recorded. Provides the temporal reference point for all volume and financial performance metrics on this record.
reference: API MPMS; Avocet Production Operations; SAP S/4HANA SD Module; COPAS

description: The minimum volume the customer is contractually obligated to take or pay for during the commitment period, expressed in the unit of measure defined by volume_uom. This is the take-or-pay (TOP) floor quantity. Failure to lift this volume triggers shortfall penalty calculations.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Scheduling Agreement; IFRS 15; COPAS; FERC Natural Gas Tariff

description: The number of calendar days prior to the delivery period start by which the customer must submit a volume nomination to the seller. Governs the commercial scheduling process and determines the latest date for volume scheduling in the supply chain.
reference: FERC Natural Gas Tariff Regulations; API MPMS; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

description: The benchmark price index to which the committed volume pricing is linked when pricing_basis is 'index_linked' or 'spot_differential' (e.g., WTI NYMEX, Brent ICE, Henry Hub NYMEX, Platts Dated Brent). Used for invoice calculation and revenue forecasting.
reference: FERC; NYMEX/CME Group; ICE; Platts; IFRS 15; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

description: The pricing mechanism governing the commercial value of volumes delivered under this commitment. 'fixed' = agreed fixed price per unit; 'index_linked' = tied to a benchmark index (e.g., WTI, Brent, Henry Hub); 'formula' = calculated via a contractual formula; 'spot_differential' = spot price plus/minus a negotiated differential.
reference: FERC Natural Gas Tariff; IFRS 15; SAP S/4HANA SD Module; COPAS

description: The number of calendar days prior to the commitment expiry date by which the customer must provide written notice to exercise the renewal option. Populated only when renewal_option_flag is True. Supports contract expiry management and commercial relationship planning.
reference: IFRS 15; SAP S/4HANA SD Module; COPAS

description: Indicates whether the term supply agreement governing this commitment includes a renewal option that the customer may exercise at or before the effective_until date. True = renewal option exists; False = no renewal option. Supports commercial contract lifecycle management and revenue forecasting.
reference: IFRS 16 Leases; IFRS 15; SAP S/4HANA SD Module; COPAS

description: The contractual penalty rate applied per unit of shortfall volume when the customer fails to meet the minimum committed volume (take-or-pay obligation). Expressed in the currency defined by currency_code per volume_uom unit. Used to calculate the shortfall penalty invoice amount.
reference: COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards; SAP S/4HANA SD Module; IFRS 15; FERC

description: The volume by which the customer's actual deliveries fall short of the minimum committed volume at the end of the commitment period, expressed in volume_uom. Calculated as max(0, min_committed_volume - delivered_volume_to_date). A positive value triggers shortfall penalty invoicing.
reference: COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards; SAP S/4HANA SD Module; IFRS 15

description: The take-or-pay (TOP) percentage of the maximum contracted volume that the customer must either lift or pay for during the commitment period. For example, 80% means the customer must take or pay for at least 80% of the maximum contracted volume. Used to derive the minimum committed volume when expressed as a percentage.
reference: COPAS Petroleum Accounting Standards; FERC Natural Gas Tariff Regulations; IFRS 15

description: The contractually permitted percentage variance (plus or minus) around the nominated or committed volume within which actual deliveries are considered compliant without triggering shortfall or excess penalties. For example, 5% means actual delivery between 95% and 105% of nominated volume is acceptable.
reference: API MPMS; SAP S/4HANA SD Module — Scheduling Agreement Tolerance; FERC

description: The contractually agreed annual percentage by which the minimum committed volume escalates (or de-escalates if negative) from one contract year to the next. Supports long-term offtake agreements with volume ramp-up provisions common in LNG and pipeline gas supply contracts.
reference: FERC Natural Gas Tariff; IFRS 15; SAP S/4HANA SD Module; COPAS

description: Unit of measure in which all volume fields (minimum committed, maximum contracted, delivered, shortfall) are expressed. BBL = Barrels, MT = Metric Tonnes, MMBTU = Million British Thermal Units, MCF = Thousand Cubic Feet, MMCF = Million Cubic Feet, BOE = Barrel of Oil Equivalent (BOE). Consistent UOM is required for contract performance monitoring and revenue forecasting.
reference: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards (MPMS); SPE PRMS; FERC

business_glossary_term: Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Framework Version
description: Version of the FATF Recommendations framework under which this KYC record was prepared and assessed (e.g., FATF 2012 Revised Recommendations, FATF 2023 Update). Ensures traceability of compliance assessments to the applicable regulatory standard version.
reference: FATF Recommendations (2012, as revised); Internal Compliance Framework Versioning Policy

description: Risk classification of the counterparty's country of incorporation based on FATF grey/black lists, OFAC sanctioned country lists, and internal country risk policy. Drives KYC tier assignment and enhanced due diligence requirements.
reference: FATF High-Risk Jurisdictions; OFAC Sanctioned Countries List; EU High-Risk Third Countries List

description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to this KYC compliance record, used for audit trails, regulatory submissions, and compliance officer tracking. Format: KYC- followed by alphanumeric characters.
reference: FATF Recommendation 10; OFAC Compliance Framework; FinCEN Customer Due Diligence Rule

description: Current lifecycle status of the KYC compliance record indicating whether the counterparty has passed, is under review, or has failed the KYC process. Drives trading eligibility and credit decisions.
reference: FATF Recommendation 10; OFAC Compliance Framework; FinCEN Customer Due Diligence Rule

business_glossary_term: Know Your Customer (KYC) Due Diligence Tier
description: Classification of the level of due diligence applied to this counterparty. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) applies to high-risk counterparties such as state-owned NOCs, PEPs, or entities in high-risk jurisdictions. Standard applies to typical IOC/trading counterparties. Simplified applies to low-risk, regulated entities.
reference: FATF Recommendation 10; FATF Recommendation 19; EU 4th Anti-Money Laundering Directive (AMLD4); FinCEN Customer Due Diligence Rule

description: Date on which the most recent periodic KYC review was completed. Distinct from verification_date (initial verification) and next_review_date (scheduled future review). Used to track review cadence compliance and identify overdue reviews.
reference: FATF Recommendation 10; Internal KYC Periodic Review Policy

description: Scheduled date for the next periodic KYC review. May differ from expiry_date if an interim review is triggered by a risk event, sanctions alert, or change in counterparty ownership structure.
reference: FATF Recommendation 10; Internal KYC Periodic Review Policy; OFAC Compliance Framework

business_glossary_term: Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Sanctions Screening Result
description: Result of screening the counterparty against the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Blocked Persons List. A confirmed match prohibits all transactions. Potential matches require compliance officer review.
reference: OFAC SDN List; 31 CFR Parts 500-598; Executive Orders on Sanctions; Internal Sanctions Compliance Policy

description: Date on which the counterparty was first onboarded into the KYC compliance program. Represents the start of the commercial relationship from a compliance perspective and anchors the KYC lifecycle timeline.
reference: FATF Recommendation 10; FinCEN Customer Due Diligence Rule; Internal Counterparty Onboarding Policy

description: Specific category of PEP classification when pep_flag is true. Distinguishes between domestic PEPs (e.g., government ministers), foreign PEPs (e.g., heads of state), international organization PEPs, close associates, and family members. Relevant for NOC counterparties with government-affiliated executives.
reference: FATF Recommendation 12; EU AMLD4 Article 3(9); FinCEN Customer Due Diligence Rule

description: Indicates whether the counterparty or any of its beneficial owners is classified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) — a current or former senior government official, state-owned enterprise executive, or close associate. PEP status mandates Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) per FATF Recommendation 12.
reference: FATF Recommendation 12; EU AMLD4 Article 20; FinCEN Customer Due Diligence Rule

description: Free-text description of the reason for KYC rejection when kyc_status is 'rejected'. Documents the specific compliance deficiency, sanctions match, or documentation failure that resulted in rejection. Required for audit trail and regulatory reporting.
reference: FATF Recommendation 10; Internal KYC Rejection Documentation Policy; SOX Section 302

description: Reason that initiated the most recent KYC review. Distinguishes between scheduled periodic reviews and event-driven reviews triggered by sanctions alerts, changes in beneficial ownership, adverse media findings, risk escalations, or regulatory requests.
reference: FATF Recommendation 10; Internal KYC Event-Driven Review Policy; OFAC Compliance Framework

description: Numeric composite risk score (0.00–100.00) calculated from the weighted combination of jurisdiction risk, AML risk rating, PEP status, sanctions exposure, adverse media findings, and beneficial ownership complexity. Higher scores indicate greater compliance risk. Used to prioritize enhanced due diligence and monitoring resources.
reference: FATF Risk-Based Approach Guidance; Internal KYC Risk Scoring Methodology; Wolfsberg Group AML Principles

description: Most recent date on which the counterparty was screened against OFAC, EU, and UN sanctions lists. Sanctions screening must be refreshed at defined intervals and upon any material change in counterparty ownership or jurisdiction.
reference: OFAC Compliance Framework; EU Consolidated Sanctions List; UN Security Council Sanctions; Internal Sanctions Screening Policy

description: Reference identifier of this KYC record in the originating compliance management system (e.g., Enablon HSE Management or dedicated KYC platform). Enables traceability from the Silver layer back to the operational system of record for audit and reconciliation purposes.
reference: Internal Data Lineage and Audit Policy; SOX Section 404; NIST Cybersecurity Framework

description: Indicates whether the counterparty is currently eligible for crude oil, natural gas, LNG, NGL, or refined product trading based on the current KYC status, sanctions screening results, AML risk rating, and document collection completeness. Set to false when KYC is expired, rejected, or sanctions match is confirmed.
reference: OFAC Compliance Framework; FATF Recommendation 10; Internal Trading Counterparty Eligibility Policy

description: Number of ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) identified and disclosed for this counterparty. A UBO is any natural person holding 25% or more direct or indirect ownership or control. Used to assess ownership complexity and completeness of beneficial ownership disclosure.
reference: FATF Recommendation 24; FinCEN Customer Due Diligence Rule 31 CFR 1010.230; EU AMLD4 Article 30

description: Result of screening the counterparty against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list. Applies globally to all counterparties regardless of jurisdiction. A confirmed match prohibits all transactions under international law.
reference: UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; UN Charter Article 41; Internal Sanctions Compliance Policy

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this KYC record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Updated on every status change, review completion, sanctions screening refresh, or document update. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.
reference: SOX Section 404; NIST Cybersecurity Framework; Internal Data Governance Audit Policy

description: Date on which the KYC verification process was completed and the counterparty's identity and documentation were confirmed by the compliance team. Marks the start of the KYC validity period.
reference: FATF Recommendation 10; FinCEN Customer Due Diligence Rule; OFAC Compliance Framework

description: Date on which the compliance waiver expires when waiver_flag is true. After this date, trading eligibility is automatically suspended until full KYC compliance is restored. Null when no waiver is in effect.
reference: Internal KYC Waiver Policy; FATF Risk-Based Approach Guidance

description: Indicates whether a formal compliance waiver has been granted for this KYC record, allowing temporary trading eligibility despite incomplete documentation or pending review. Waivers require senior compliance authority approval and are time-limited.
reference: Internal KYC Waiver Policy; FATF Risk-Based Approach Guidance; SOX Section 302

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each license interest record representing a counterparty's participation in an operating license.
Foreign key linking to the counterparty who holds an interest in the operating license. Represents the participant in the PSA/JOA agreement.
Foreign key to customer_counterparty. Identifies the participant holding the interest.
Foreign key linking to the operating license in which the counterparty holds an interest. Represents the licensed area or facility covered by the participation agreement.
Timestamp when this license interest record was created in the system. Used for audit and data lineage purposes.
Date on which this counterparty's interest in the operating license became effective. Used for temporal tracking of ownership changes, farm-ins, and farm-outs.

Date on which this counterparty's interest in the operating license expires or was terminated. Null indicates current active interest. Used for tracking historical participation and ownership transitions.

Indicates whether this counterparty is a signatory to the Joint Operating Agreement (JOA) governing this license. Non-signatory participants may hold interests through assignment or farm-in agreements.
Timestamp when this license interest record was last modified. Used for audit and change tracking purposes.

The counterparty's net revenue interest percentage in this specific operating license. Represents the share of production revenue after royalties and other burdens. Used for production entitlement calculations.

Indicates whether this counterparty is the designated operator for this operating license. The operator is responsible for day-to-day operations and typically has the largest working interest. Only one participant per license should have operator_flag = true.

Current status of the counterparty's participation in this operating license. ACTIVE indicates current participation with entitlement to production. SUSPENDED indicates temporary halt due to regulatory or contractual issues. TERMINATED indicates participation has ended. PENDING indicates interest is under negotiation or regulatory approval.

Indicates whether this counterparty's interest has reached payout under the PSA or JOA terms. PRE_PAYOUT means capital costs are still being recovered. POST_PAYOUT means capital has been recovered and different revenue sharing terms apply. NOT_APPLICABLE for licenses without payout provisions.

The counterparty's working interest percentage in this specific operating license. Represents the share of capital expenditure and operating costs borne by this participant. Sum of all working interests for a license typically equals 100%.
Unique identifier for the customer tax registration record. Primary key for the tax registration entity.

Foreign key linking to customer.account. Business justification: Tax registrations can be account-specific in multi-jurisdiction scenarios. Different accounts under the same counterparty may operate in different tax jurisdictions with separate registration requirem
Reference to the customer counterparty entity for which this tax registration applies. Links to the customer master data.
Employee identifier of the tax compliance officer responsible for verifying and maintaining this tax registration record.

Internal approval workflow status for this tax registration record: draft (being prepared), pending_review (awaiting approval), approved (validated and active), rejected (failed validation).
Date and time when this tax registration record was approved. Used for audit trail and compliance reporting.
Date and time when this tax registration record was first created in the system. Audit trail for record lifecycle.
Reference identifier or URI to the stored tax registration documentation in the document management system. Enables retrieval of supporting documents for audit.
Date from which this tax registration becomes valid and should be applied to invoices and payments. Start of the registration validity period.
Date when this tax registration expires or is no longer valid. Null for open-ended registrations. System must not apply this registration after this date.
Name of the government tax authority or agency that issued this registration (e.g., IRS, HMRC, ATO). Provides context for registration validation.
Three-letter ISO country code identifying the tax jurisdiction where this registration is valid. Critical for determining applicable tax treaties and withholding rates.
State, province, or sub-national jurisdiction where the tax registration applies. Relevant for federal systems with state-level taxation (e.g., USA, Canada).
Date when the tax registration details were last verified with the tax authority or through official documentation. Used for compliance audit trail.

business_glossary_term: Legal Entity Name for Tax Registration
description: The official legal name of the customer entity as registered with the tax authority. Must match tax documentation exactly for compliance.
Scheduled date for the next periodic review and verification of tax registration details. Ensures ongoing compliance with tax regulations.
Free-text field for additional comments, special instructions, or context regarding this tax registration. Used for documenting exceptions or special handling requirements.
Indicates whether the customer has a permanent establishment in the jurisdiction. True if PE exists, affecting tax treaty application and withholding requirements.
City of the registered address on file with the tax authority.
Three-letter ISO country code of the registered address on file with the tax authority.
First line of the registered address on file with the tax authority. Required for tax correspondence and compliance verification.
Postal or ZIP code of the registered address on file with the tax authority.
Date when the customer was officially registered with the tax authority in this jurisdiction. Historical record of initial registration.
The unique tax registration number or business identifier assigned by the tax authority in the jurisdiction. This is the externally-known identifier for tax purposes.

Current lifecycle status of the tax registration: active (valid and in use), inactive (not currently used), suspended (temporarily halted by authority), pending (awaiting approval), expired (validity period ended), or revoked (cancelled by authority).
The category of tax registration: TIN (Tax Identification Number), VAT (Value Added Tax), GST (Goods and Services Tax), sales tax, withholding tax, or excise tax registration.
Explanation of why the tax registration was rejected during approval workflow. Null if approved or pending.
Code identifying the source system from which this tax registration record originated (e.g., SAP, Oracle, legacy system). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.
Unique identifier or key of this tax registration record in the source system. Enables traceability back to the system of record.
Reference number of the tax exemption certificate issued by the tax authority. Required for audit trail when applying tax exemptions to petroleum product sales.
Date when the tax exemption certificate expires. System must revert to standard tax treatment after this date unless renewed.
Indicates whether the customer holds a valid tax exemption certificate for this jurisdiction. True if exempt, false otherwise.
Date when the tax form or supporting documentation was received from the customer. Used for compliance audit trail.
Type of tax form or documentation on file (e.g., W-9, W-8BEN, W-8BEN-E, VAT certificate). Indicates the nature of tax documentation supporting this registration.

The primary tax identification number assigned by the national tax authority. Used for income tax reporting and withholding compliance. May be the same as registration_number for TIN-type registrations.
Three-letter ISO country code of the customers tax residency. Determines treaty benefit eligibility and withholding tax obligations for cross-border petroleum transactions.
Specific article or section of the tax treaty that grants the withholding rate reduction or exemption. Used for compliance documentation.
Indicates whether the customer is eligible for reduced withholding tax rates under a bilateral tax treaty. True if eligible, false otherwise.
Three-letter ISO country code of the tax treaty that provides benefit eligibility. Null if no treaty applies.
VAT or GST registration number issued by the tax authority. Required for VAT invoice issuance and input tax credit claims on petroleum product sales.
The applicable withholding tax rate percentage for payments to this customer in this jurisdiction. Used to calculate tax withholding on invoices and payments for cross-border petroleum sales.

Business identifier for the curative action, typically assigned by the land department for tracking and reference purposes.
Current lifecycle status of the curative action. Tracks progress from identification through resolution.

Estimated cost to complete the curative action, including legal fees, recording fees, landman time, and any consideration paid to resolve the defect.
General Ledger (GL) account code for posting curative action costs in the financial system.

Business priority assigned to the curative action based on drilling schedule, capital commitment, and operational impact. Critical priority typically indicates pre-drilling requirement.
Date when the curative instrument was officially recorded in the county land records office.

business_glossary_term: Scope 1 Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions (Metric Tonnes CO2e)
description: Total direct Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions from sources owned or controlled by the company during the reporting period, expressed in metric tonnes of CO2 equivalent (CO2e). Includes combustion of fuels in company-owned equipment, flaring, venting, and fugitive emissions. Required by EPA GHG Reporting Rule and SEC climate disclosure rules.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 98; GHG Protocol Corporate Standard; GRI 305-1; SASB EM-EP-110a.1; SEC Climate Disclosure Rules

business_glossary_term: Scope 2 Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions (Metric Tonnes CO2e)
description: Total indirect GHG emissions from the generation of purchased electricity, steam, heat, or cooling consumed by the company during the reporting period, expressed in metric tonnes CO2e. Reported on both location-based and market-based methods per GHG Protocol.
reference: GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance; GRI 305-2; SASB EM-EP-110a.1; EPA 40 CFR Part 98; SEC Climate Disclosure Rules

business_glossary_term: Scope 3 Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions (Metric Tonnes CO2e)
description: Total value-chain indirect GHG emissions not included in Scope 2, expressed in metric tonnes CO2e. For oil and gas, the dominant Scope 3 category is Category 11 (use of sold products — combustion of sold hydrocarbons by end customers). Voluntary under most frameworks but increasingly required by investors and regulators.
reference: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard; GRI 305-3; TCFD Recommendations; SEC Climate Disclosure Rules

description: Total monetary value of voluntary social investment and community development expenditures during the reporting period, expressed in US dollars. Includes community programs, local content spending, education, and infrastructure contributions. Reported per GRI 413 and API ESG framework.
reference: GRI 413-1; API ESG Disclosure Framework; SASB; ISO 26000

description: Indicates whether the internal controls over ESG data collection and reporting have been verified as part of the SOX compliance program. Supports integration of ESG metrics into financial reporting internal control frameworks.
reference: Sarbanes-Oxley Act Section 302 and 404; SEC Climate Disclosure Rules; COSO Framework

description: Total number of hydrocarbon spills to the environment (land or water) above the reportable threshold during the reporting period. Includes crude oil, refined products, and chemical spills. Required by BSEE, EPA, and PHMSA reporting obligations.
reference: BSEE 30 CFR Part 254; EPA 40 CFR Part 112; PHMSA 49 CFR Part 195; GRI 306-3; SASB EM-EP-160a.1

description: Total volume of hydrocarbons spilled to the environment during the reporting period, expressed in barrels (bbls). Distinct from spill count — captures severity of spill events. Required by BSEE, EPA, and PHMSA.
reference: BSEE 30 CFR Part 254; EPA 40 CFR Part 112; PHMSA 49 CFR Part 195; GRI 306-3; SASB EM-EP-160a.1

description: Total number of hours worked by all employees and contractors during the reporting period. Used as the denominator for calculating TRIR, LTIR, and other safety rate metrics. Required by OSHA and API safety reporting standards.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR Part 1904; API RP 97; GRI 403-9; SASB EM-EP-320a.1

description: Total number of employees (full-time and part-time) employed by the reporting entity at the end of the reporting period. Excludes contractors unless otherwise noted. Required by GRI 2-7 and SASB social metrics.
reference: GRI 2-7; SASB EM-EP-320a.1; SEC Regulation S-K Human Capital Disclosure

description: Total Recordable Incident Rate (TRIR) for the reporting period, calculated as (number of recordable incidents × 200,000) / total hours worked. Industry-standard OSHA safety metric reported per API RP 97 and required in ESG disclosures. Lower values indicate better safety performance.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR Part 1904; API RP 97; GRI 403-9; SASB EM-EP-320a.1

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this ESG report record. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: SOX Internal Controls; GRI Standards; Enablon HSE Management

description: Total volume of natural gas intentionally vented to the atmosphere during the reporting period, expressed in million standard cubic feet (MMscf). Venting is separately tracked from flaring per EPA and BSEE requirements and is a key component of Scope 1 GHG emissions.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 98 Subpart W; BSEE; SASB EM-EP-110a.1; GRI 305-1

description: Total volume of water recycled or reused within operations during the reporting period, expressed in cubic metres. Demonstrates water efficiency and circular water management practices. Tracked per GRI 303 and SASB water metrics.
reference: GRI 303-3; SASB EM-EP-140a.1; API ESG Disclosure Framework

description: Total volume of water withdrawn from all sources (surface water, groundwater, produced water, municipal supply) during the reporting period, expressed in cubic metres. Key water stewardship metric per GRI 303 and SASB EM-EP-140a.1.
reference: GRI 303-3; SASB EM-EP-140a.1; API ESG Disclosure Framework; EPA Clean Water Act

description: Percentage of senior management and board-level positions held by women at the end of the reporting period. Tracks gender diversity at leadership levels, a distinct metric from overall workforce gender diversity per GRI 405-1.
reference: GRI 405-1; SEC Regulation S-K Human Capital Disclosure; TCFD Governance Pillar; API ESG Disclosure Framework

description: Percentage of total workforce that identifies as women at the end of the reporting period. Key diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) metric required by GRI 405-1 and increasingly by institutional investors and ESG rating agencies.
reference: GRI 405-1; SASB; SEC Regulation S-K Human Capital Disclosure; API ESG Disclosure Framework

business_glossary_term: Actual Production Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
description: The actual average daily crude oil production volume reported for the quota period, expressed in BOPD. Sourced from OSIsoft PI System production historian and Avocet Production Operations daily allocation data. This is the figure submitted to the OPEC Secretariat.
reference: OPEC Secretariat Monthly Production Survey; Avocet Production Operations; OSIsoft PI System

business_glossary_term: Allocated Quota Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
description: The official OPEC-assigned production quota for the member country or company for the quota period, expressed in Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD). This is the baseline entitlement as communicated by the OPEC Secretariat and forms the compliance benchmark.
reference: OPEC Ministerial Conference Decisions; OPEC Secretariat Quota Notification; SEC Reserves Disclosure Rules

description: The date on which the quota position record was formally approved by the designated approver for submission to the OPEC Secretariat. Part of the SOX-compliant internal control audit trail.

description: Name or employee identifier of the senior manager or executive who approved the production report and quota compliance position for submission to the OPEC Secretariat. Supports SOX internal control documentation.
reference: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX); Internal Compliance Governance Framework

business_glossary_term: Baseline Reference Production Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
description: The reference production level (in BOPD) used by OPEC as the baseline from which quota cuts or increases are calculated. Typically corresponds to a specific historical production month agreed upon in the ministerial conference decision.
reference: OPEC Ministerial Conference Decisions; OPEC Secretariat Quota Notification

business_glossary_term: Compensation Plan Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
description: The agreed additional production curtailment (in BOPD below quota) committed by the member for the current period as part of a formal compensation plan to offset prior overproduction. Null if no compensation plan is active.
reference: OPEC Ministerial Conference Decisions; OPEC Secretariat Compensation Plan Notification

description: Name of the designated compliance officer or regulatory affairs manager responsible for overseeing OPEC quota compliance for this period. Used for accountability tracking and regulatory correspondence.
reference: Internal Compliance Governance Framework; SOX Internal Controls

description: Current compliance status of the quota position for the period. 'compliant' = production within quota; 'overproduced' = production exceeds quota; 'underproduced' = production below quota; 'pending_verification' = awaiting final production data; 'disputed' = member disputes OPEC assessment; 'compensating' = member is executing a compensation plan for prior overproduction.
reference: OPEC Secretariat Compliance Monitoring Framework; OPEC Statute

description: Indicates whether natural gas condensate volumes have been excluded from the reported production figure in accordance with OPEC quota measurement conventions. True = condensate excluded; False = condensate included. OPEC quotas historically apply to crude oil only, excluding condensate.
reference: OPEC Secretariat Quota Measurement Conventions; OPEC Ministerial Conference Decisions

description: Official reference number or identifier of the OPEC Ministerial Conference decision that established or last amended the quota allocation for this period (e.g., Decision 178 of the 186th Extraordinary Meeting). Provides traceability to the governing OPEC resolution.

description: The timestamp when this OPEC quota position record was first created in the Silver Layer data product, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides the audit creation trail required for SOX compliance and data lineage.

description: API or industry-standard code identifying the crude oil grade or stream included in the production volume (e.g., Arab Light, Basrah Heavy, Bonny Light). Relevant where OPEC quota applies to specific crude streams or where condensate exclusions apply.
reference: American Petroleum Institute (API) Crude Classification; OPEC Secretariat Reporting Framework

business_glossary_term: Cumulative Overproduction Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
description: The running cumulative overproduction volume (in BOPD) carried forward from prior periods that has not yet been compensated through production curtailment. A non-zero value triggers a compensation obligation under OPEC ministerial decisions.
reference: OPEC Ministerial Conference Decisions; OPEC Secretariat Compliance Monitoring Framework

description: Status of the internal production curtailment plan developed to ensure compliance with the OPEC quota for this period. 'not_required' = production within quota; 'planned' = curtailment plan drafted; 'active' = curtailment being executed; 'completed' = curtailment achieved; 'deferred' = curtailment postponed.
reference: Internal Compliance Reporting Standards; OPEC Secretariat Compliance Monitoring Framework

business_glossary_term: Production Curtailment Target Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
description: The planned production reduction (in BOPD) required to bring actual production into compliance with the effective quota. Derived from the curtailment plan and used to guide field-level production scheduling decisions.

business_glossary_term: Effective Quota Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)

reference: OPEC Ministerial Conference Decisions; OPEC Secretariat Voluntary Cut Notification

reference: SOX Section 302; ISO 55001 Asset Management; NIST Cybersecurity Framework

description: Date and time when the release was first discovered or detected by company personnel, SCADA system, or third party. May differ from incident_datetime (when the release actually began). The discovery timestamp is the trigger point for regulatory notification deadline clocks under CERCLA, EPCRA, and OPA 90.
reference: CERCLA Section 103(a); EPCRA Section 304(b); OPA 90 Section 4201; EPA 40 CFR Part 302.6

description: Reference identifier linking this regulatory release report to the corresponding incident record in the Enablon HSE Management system, which serves as the operational system of record for HSE incident management, permit to work, and environmental compliance tracking. Enables cross-system traceability between the compliance data product and the source HSE system.
reference: Enablon HSE Management system integration; ISO 14001 Environmental Management System; OSHA 29 CFR 1904 recordkeeping

reference: EPA Facility Registry Service (FRS); BSEE 30 CFR Part 254; API RP 75 Offshore Safety

business_glossary_term: Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emission in CO2 Equivalent Tonnes
description: Estimated greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in CO2 equivalent tonnes resulting from the release event, applicable for gas releases (methane, VOCs) subject to EPA GHG reporting under 40 CFR Part 98. Required for ESG environmental disclosure, EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP), and OPEC/IEA emissions tracking.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 98 GHGRP; GHG Protocol Corporate Standard; ESG reporting frameworks; SEC climate disclosure rules

business_glossary_term: Environmental Release Incident Date and Time
description: Date and time when the environmental release event occurred or was first detected, recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. This is the principal real-world event timestamp used for regulatory notification deadline calculations and compliance reporting. Satisfies BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 302.6; CERCLA Section 103; EPCRA Section 304(b)

description: Detailed narrative description of the environmental release incident including circumstances, sequence of events, immediate response actions taken, and any relevant operational context. Used for regulatory submission narratives, internal investigation reports, and ESG disclosure summaries.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 112; BSEE 30 CFR Part 254; EPCRA Section 304(c) written follow-up report requirements

description: Externally-known, human-readable identifier assigned to the environmental release incident at the time of initial notification. Used for cross-referencing with regulatory agency submissions, Enablon HSE Management incident records, and internal compliance tracking. Satisfies BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 302; EPCRA Section 304; Enablon HSE Management incident numbering convention

business_glossary_term: Initial Regulatory Notification Date and Time
description: Date and time when the initial verbal or written notification was made to the National Response Center (NRC), EPA, BSEE, state agency, or other required regulatory body. Used to calculate notification timeliness compliance against the regulatory deadline (typically within 24 hours of discovery for CERCLA/EPCRA).
reference: CERCLA Section 103(a) — 24-hour NRC notification; EPCRA Section 304(b); OPA 90 Section 4201; BSEE 30 CFR Part 254.46

description: Geographic latitude coordinate (decimal degrees, WGS84 datum) of the release location. Required for GIS mapping, spill trajectory modeling, regulatory notification forms, and emergency response dispatch. Positive values indicate North latitude.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 112 SPCC; OPA 90; BSEE 30 CFR Part 254; WGS84 datum standard

description: Geographic longitude coordinate (decimal degrees, WGS84 datum) of the release location. Required for GIS mapping, spill trajectory modeling, regulatory notification forms, and emergency response dispatch. Negative values indicate West longitude.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 112 SPCC; OPA 90; BSEE 30 CFR Part 254; WGS84 datum standard

business_glossary_term: Regulatory Notification Deadline Date and Time
description: Calculated deadline by which the initial regulatory notification must be made, based on discovery_datetime plus the applicable regulatory timeframe (e.g., 24 hours for CERCLA NRC notification, 15 minutes for BSEE offshore spills). Used for compliance monitoring and deadline tracking.
reference: CERCLA Section 103(a); EPCRA Section 304(b); BSEE 30 CFR Part 254.46; OPA 90

description: Boolean flag indicating whether the initial regulatory notification was made within the required timeframe. A value of False indicates a potential regulatory violation requiring documentation of root cause and corrective action. Critical for compliance audit and penalty risk assessment.
reference: CERCLA Section 103; EPCRA Section 304; BSEE 30 CFR Part 254; EPA enforcement policy

description: Report number assigned by the National Response Center (NRC) upon receipt of the initial verbal notification for releases meeting CERCLA or OPA 90 reportable quantity thresholds. Serves as the official federal tracking number for the spill notification and is required on follow-up written reports.
reference: CERCLA Section 103; OPA 90 Section 4201; NRC — U.S. Coast Guard operated; EPA 40 CFR Part 302.6

description: Boolean flag indicating whether the release occurred on an offshore facility (OCS — Outer Continental Shelf) subject to BSEE and BOEM jurisdiction, as opposed to onshore facilities regulated by EPA and state agencies. Determines applicable regulatory reporting pathway and notification recipients.
reference: BSEE 30 CFR Part 254; BOEM 30 CFR Part 550; OPA 90 Section 4201; Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act

description: Quantity of the released substance that was recovered through containment, skimming, vacuum recovery, or other response measures, expressed in the same unit as release_quantity_unit. Net environmental impact is calculated as release_quantity minus recovered_quantity. Required for OPA 90 and BSEE spill response reporting.
reference: OPA 90 Section 4201; BSEE 30 CFR Part 254; EPA 40 CFR Part 112; NCP — National Contingency Plan

description: Primary regulatory agency to which the release report is submitted or notified. Determines the applicable reporting form, submission portal, and regulatory requirements. Multiple agencies may be notified for a single incident; this field captures the primary lead agency.
